writer.name: William Shakespeare
writer.bio: English playwright and poet, 1564 to 1616. A glover's son from Stratford with no university education, he went to London, acted, and wrote about 38 plays for a working theatre company he part owned.

works.title: The Plays
works.note: Written between about 1590 and 1613 for the stage, to be heard, not read. Many lines are spoken by villains and fools, so the speaker is not always the author's view.

works.title: The Sonnets
works.note: 154 sonnets printed in 1609, most of them probably written in the 1590s. Many are about time, age and what lasts.

quotes.text: Moderate lamentation is the right of the dead; excessive grief the enemy to the living.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Grieve in measure. Too much grief hurts the living more than it honors the dead.

quotes.text:
Love all, trust a few,
Do wrong to none. Be able for thine enemy
Rather in power than use; and keep thy friend
Under thy own life’s key. Be check’d for silence,
But never tax’d for speech.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Love widely, trust slowly, hurt no one, and keep your friends close. Say less than you could.

quotes.text:
Our remedies oft in ourselves do lie,
Which we ascribe to heaven: the fated sky
Gives us free scope; only doth backward pull
Our slow designs when we ourselves are dull.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: You blame the stars, but mostly you are the thing holding you back.

quotes.text:
Impossible be strange attempts to those
That weigh their pains in sense, and do suppose
What hath been cannot be.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Impossible things only look that way to people who count the cost of trying.

quotes.text:
Oft expectation fails, and most oft there
Where most it promises; and oft it hits
Where hope is coldest, and despair most fits.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 2 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Expected wins often fail, and the long shots land where hope was lowest. Keep going.

quotes.text:
Good alone
Is good without a name; vileness is so:
The property by what it is should go,
Not by the title. She is young, wise, fair;
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 2 Scene 3
quotes.plain: A thing is what it is, not what it is called. Judge by the substance, not the title.

quotes.text:
I have felt so many quirks of joy and grief
That the first face of neither on the start
Can woman me unto ’t.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 3 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Real hardship has taught her not to be thrown by the first look of joy or grief.

quotes.text:
’Tis not the many oaths that makes the truth,
But the plain single vow that is vow’d true.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 2
quotes.plain: One vow kept beats a thousand oaths sworn.

quotes.text: Now, God delay our rebellion! As we are ourselves, what things are we!
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Admit it: we are our own worst enemy, and we know it.

quotes.text: The web of our life is of a mingled yarn, good and ill together; our virtues would be proud if our faults whipped them not; and our crimes would despair if they were not cherish’d by our virtues.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Life is good and bad woven together. Wins keep you humble, flaws keep you from despair.

quotes.text:
Simply the thing I am
Shall make me live.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Just being what I am is enough to keep me going.

quotes.text:
But with the word the time will bring on summer,
When briers shall have leaves as well as thorns,
And be as sweet as sharp.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Be patient. Summer is coming, and the thorns will have leaves too.

quotes.text:
All’s well that ends well; still the fine’s the crown.
Whate’er the course, the end is the renown.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 4
quotes.plain: If it ends well, the rough road was worth it. The finish is what counts.

quotes.text:
Let’s take the instant by the forward top;
For we are old, and on our quick’st decrees
Th’inaudible and noiseless foot of time
Steals ere we can effect them.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 5 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Grab the moment now. Time moves silently and steals the thing you meant to do.

quotes.text:
Our rash faults
Make trivial price of serious things we have,
Not knowing them until we know their grave.
quotes.location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 5 Scene 3
quotes.plain: We treat what we have as cheap until it is gone.

quotes.text: There’s beggary in the love that can be reckoned.
quotes.plain: Love you can put a number on is not much of a love.

quotes.text:
Let Rome in Tiber melt, and the wide arch
Of the ranged empire fall! Here is my space.
Kingdoms are clay. Our dungy earth alike
Feeds beast as man.
quotes.plain: Empires are dust. We all end up the same earth, so what you build with people matters more.

quotes.text: The nature of bad news infects the teller.
quotes.plain: Bringing bad news earns you the blame. People punish the messenger.

quotes.text: Things that are past are done with me. ’Tis thus:
quotes.plain: The past is finished with me. I deal with what is in front of me.

quotes.text:
Who tells me true, though in his tale lie death,
I hear him as he flattered.
quotes.plain: Tell me the truth even if it hurts. I would rather hear it than be flattered.

quotes.text:
O, then we bring forth weeds
When our quick minds lie still, and our ills told us
Is as our earing. Fare thee well awhile.
quotes.plain: Without hard truths, the mind goes to seed. Criticism is the plowing that keeps it growing.

quotes.text: In time we hate that which we often fear.
quotes.plain: We come to hate what we keep fearing.

quotes.text:
My salad days,
When I was green in judgment, cold in blood,
To say as I said then.
quotes.plain: Looking back on the fool you were at twenty. You were green and sure of yourself.

quotes.text:
Whiles we are suitors to their throne, decays
The thing we sue for.
quotes.plain: Waiting and begging for a thing can make it wither before it arrives.

quotes.text:
We, ignorant of ourselves,
Beg often our own harms, which the wise powers
Deny us for our good; so find we profit
By losing of our prayers.
quotes.plain: We often pray for what would hurt us. Some unanswered prayers were a favor.

quotes.text:
Caesar gets money where
He loses hearts.
quotes.plain: Some people win cash and lose loyalty. The trade is not worth it.

quotes.text:
Age cannot wither her, nor custom stale
Her infinite variety. Other women cloy
The appetites they feed, but she makes hungry
Where most she satisfies.
quotes.plain: Real pull never fades. Other things feed the hunger, she keeps you hungry.

quotes.text:
Well, I know not
What counts harsh Fortune casts upon my face,
But in my bosom shall she never come
To make my heart her vassal.
quotes.plain: Fortune can hit my face, but it never gets my heart.

quotes.text: If he do, sure he cannot weep ’t back again.
quotes.plain: You can't cry your fortune back once you've laughed it away.

quotes.text:
Who seeks, and will not take when once ’tis offered,
Shall never find it more.
quotes.plain: Hesitate when the chance is offered and it won't come twice.

quotes.text:
Be you not troubled with the time, which drives
O’er your content these strong necessities,
But let determined things to destiny
Hold unbewailed their way.
quotes.plain: Don't fret over what has to happen. Let it run its course.

quotes.text:
Celerity is never more admired
Than by the negligent.
quotes.plain: Speed only impresses people who are slow.

quotes.text:
Fortune knows
We scorn her most when most she offers blows.
quotes.plain: The harder fate hits, the more you can laugh in its face.

quotes.text:
I see men’s judgments are
A parcel of their fortunes, and things outward
Do draw the inward quality after them
To suffer all alike.
quotes.plain: When luck turns, even your judgment goes with it.

quotes.text:
The loyalty well held to fools does make
Our faith mere folly. Yet he that can endure
To follow with allegiance a fallen lord
Does conquer him that did his master conquer,
And earns a place i’ th’ story.
quotes.plain: Staying loyal to someone who is falling is what earns a name.

quotes.text:
There’s sap in’t yet. The next time I do fight
I’ll make Death love me, for I will contend
Even with his pestilent scythe.
quotes.plain: Still got sap in me. I'll make Death respect me.

quotes.text:
When valour preys on reason,
It eats the sword it fights with.
quotes.plain: Courage that kills your reasoning wrecks the weapon it fights with.

quotes.text:
Never anger
Made good guard for itself.
quotes.plain: Anger never protected anybody.

quotes.text:
That which is now a horse, even with a thought
The rack dislimns and makes it indistinct
As water is in water.
quotes.plain: What looks solid dissolves as fast as a thought.

quotes.text:
Nay, good my fellows, do not please sharp fate
To grace it with your sorrows. Bid that welcome
Which comes to punish us, and we punish it,
Seeming to bear it lightly. Take me up.
quotes.plain: Take hard fate lightly and it loses some of its bite.

quotes.text:
Our size of sorrow,
Proportioned to our cause, must be as great
As that which makes it.
quotes.plain: Grief should be as big as what caused it. Don't shrink it for anyone.

quotes.text:
Not Caesar’s valour hath o’erthrown Antony,
But Antony’s hath triumphed on itself.
quotes.plain: Nobody beat him but himself.

quotes.text:
His legs bestrid the ocean; his reared arm
Crested the world; his voice was propertied
As all the tuned spheres, and that to friends;
But when he meant to quail and shake the orb,
He was as rattling thunder.
quotes.plain: Some people loom over the whole world, gentle with friends and thunder when crossed.

quotes.text: Make not your thoughts your prisons. No, dear queen;
quotes.plain: Don't turn your own thoughts into your prison.

quotes.text: The more pity that fools may not speak wisely what wise men do foolishly.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 1 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Fools get laughed at for the same things wise men do and call smart.

quotes.text:
Sweet are the uses of adversity,
Which, like the toad, ugly and venomous,
Wears yet a precious jewel in his head;
And this our life, exempt from public haunt,
Finds tongues in trees, books in the running brooks,
Sermons in stones, and good in everything.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Hard times are teachers in disguise, and there's something good in everything.

quotes.text:
Thou art not for the fashion of these times,
Where none will sweat but for promotion,
And having that do choke their service up
Even with the having. It is not so with thee.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Most people only work for the promotion, and the prize kills the effort.

quotes.text: But as all is mortal in nature, so is all nature in love mortal in folly.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Everything natural dies, and everything in love goes foolish.

quotes.text: Nay, I shall ne’er be ware of mine own wit till I break my shins against it.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 4
quotes.plain: You don't see your own blind spot until you crash into it.

quotes.text:
’Tis but an hour ago since it was nine,
And after one hour more ’twill be eleven.
And so from hour to hour we ripe and ripe,
And then from hour to hour we rot and rot,
And thereby hangs a tale.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7
quotes.plain: Hour by hour we ripen, then we rot. That's all the story.

quotes.text:
Thou seest we are not all alone unhappy.
This wide and universal theatre
Presents more woeful pageants than the scene
Wherein we play in.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7
quotes.plain: Your pain isn't unique. The world is full of worse stages.

quotes.text:
All the world’s a stage,
And all the men and women merely players;
They have their exits and their entrances,
And one man in his time plays many parts,
His acts being seven ages.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7
quotes.plain: Everyone plays many parts in a short run, then exits.

quotes.text:
Last scene of all,
That ends this strange eventful history,
Is second childishness and mere oblivion,
Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 2 Scene 7
quotes.plain: The last act is second childhood, then nothing.

quotes.text: I earn that I eat, get that I wear, owe no man hate, envy no man’s happiness, glad of other men’s good, content with my harm; and the greatest of my pride is to see my ewes graze and my lambs suck.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Earn what you eat, envy no one, and be proud of simple work.

quotes.text: I will chide no breather in the world but myself, against whom I know most faults.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Blame yourself first. You know your faults best.

quotes.text: Time travels in divers paces with divers persons. I’ll tell you who time ambles withal, who time trots withal, who time gallops withal, and who he stands still withal.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Time moves at a different speed for everyone.

quotes.text: Love is merely a madness, and, I tell you, deserves as well a dark house and a whip as madmen do; and the reason why they are not so punished and cured is that the lunacy is so ordinary that the whippers are in love too.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Love is madness, and nobody punishes it because everyone has it.

quotes.text: But all’s brave that youth mounts and folly guides. Who comes here?
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Everything looks brave when youth rides and folly steers.

quotes.text: Sell when you can; you are not for all markets.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 3 Scene 5
quotes.plain: Take the offer while it exists. Your value is not for everyone, and it will not last forever.

quotes.text: Then to have seen much and to have nothing is to have rich eyes and poor hands.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Experience without anything built from it is just sightseeing.

quotes.text: Men have died from time to time and worms have eaten them, but not for love.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Heartbreak feels fatal and never is. People get over it.

quotes.text: Why then, can one desire too much of a good thing?
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Even good things can be wanted past the point of sense.

quotes.text: Well, Time is the old justice that examines all such offenders, and let time try.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Time tests everyone in the end. Let it sort out who is real.

quotes.text:
Twice did he turn his back and purposed so;
But kindness, nobler ever than revenge,
And nature, stronger than his just occasion,
Made him give battle to the lioness,
Who quickly fell before him; in which hurtling
From miserable slumber I awaked.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 3
quotes.plain: He had every reason to walk away from his enemy. Kindness beat revenge.

quotes.text:
’Twas I; but ’tis not I. I do not shame
To tell you what I was, since my conversion
So sweetly tastes, being the thing I am.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 4 Scene 3
quotes.plain: You can be ashamed of who you were and still be proud of who you became.

quotes.text: The fool doth think he is wise, but the wise man knows himself to be a fool.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 1
quotes.plain: The less you know, the surer you feel. Real wisdom starts with knowing how little you know.

quotes.text: But O, how bitter a thing it is to look into happiness through another man’s eyes!
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Watching someone else get what you want hurts more than not having it.

quotes.text:
I sometimes do believe and sometimes do not,
As those that fear they hope, and know they fear.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Hope and fear arrive together. You can want something so badly you are scared to believe in it.

quotes.text: Rich honesty dwells like a miser, sir, in a poor house, as your pearl in your foul oyster.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Something valuable can live in a plain, unimpressive package.

quotes.text: He uses his folly like a stalking-horse, and under the presentation of that he shoots his wit.
quotes.location: As You Like It, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: The sharpest people hide behind looking foolish and strike from there.

quotes.text:
He that commends me to mine own content
Commends me to the thing I cannot get.
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 1 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Being told to just be content is advice to go get the one thing you cannot find.

quotes.text:
I to the world am like a drop of water
That in the ocean seeks another drop,
Who, failing there to find his fellow forth,
Unseen, inquisitive, confounds himself.
So I, to find a mother and a brother,
In quest of them, unhappy, lose myself.
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 1 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Searching for someone else can make you lose track of yourself.

quotes.text:
A wretched soul bruis’d with adversity,
We bid be quiet when we hear it cry;
But were we burd’ned with like weight of pain,
As much, or more, we should ourselves complain:
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 2 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Telling someone to stay calm is easy when it is not your pain.

quotes.text:
When the sun shines let foolish gnats make sport,
But creep in crannies when he hides his beams.
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 2 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Fair-weather people show up when things are good and vanish when they are not.

quotes.text:
Am I in earth, in heaven, or in hell?
Sleeping or waking, mad, or well-advis’d?
Known unto these, and to myself disguis’d!
I’ll say as they say, and persever so,
And in this mist at all adventures go.
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 2 Scene 2
quotes.plain: When nothing makes sense, keep moving and let it clear as you go.

quotes.text:
Time is a very bankrupt, and owes more than he’s worth to season.
Nay, he’s a thief too. Have you not heard men say
That time comes stealing on by night and day?
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 4 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Time quietly takes everything, and it owes you nothing.

quotes.text:
Sweet recreation barr’d, what doth ensue
But moody and dull melancholy,
Kinsman to grim and comfortless despair,
And at her heels a huge infectious troop
Of pale distemperatures and foes to life?
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 5 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Cut out rest and play and what follows is gloom, then despair, then sickness.

quotes.text:
In food, in sport, and life-preserving rest
To be disturb’d would mad or man or beast.
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 5 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Take away food, play and sleep and anyone will crack.

quotes.text:
O! grief hath chang’d me since you saw me last,
And careful hours with time’s deformed hand,
Have written strange defeatures in my face.
quotes.location: The Comedy of Errors, Act 5 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Worry and years change your face until people stop recognizing you.

quotes.text:
Who deserves greatness
Deserves your hate; and your affections are
A sick man’s appetite, who desires most that
Which would increase his evil.
quotes.plain: Anyone great gets hated. And people often crave exactly what makes them worse.

quotes.text:
He that depends
Upon your favours swims with fins of lead,
And hews down oaks with rushes.
quotes.plain: Live on other people's approval and you are swimming with weights and chopping trees with reeds.

quotes.text:
With every minute you do change a mind
And call him noble that was now your hate,
Him vile that was your garland.
quotes.plain: The crowd flips on you every minute. Their praise and their hate are both weather.

quotes.text:
Now put your shields before your hearts, and fight
With hearts more proof than shields.
quotes.plain: Armor helps, but a tougher heart is what holds.

quotes.text:
Sir, praise me not.
My work hath yet not warmed me.
quotes.plain: Do not clap for me yet. I have barely started.

quotes.text:
He that has but effected his good will
Hath overta’en mine act.
quotes.plain: Someone who simply did what they meant to do has matched anything I did.

quotes.text:
You shall not be
The grave of your deserving.
quotes.plain: Do not bury your own worth by hiding it.

quotes.text: Why, ’tis no great matter; for a very little thief of occasion will rob you of a great deal of patience.
quotes.plain: Small annoyances steal your patience if you let them. Do not hand it over that cheap.

quotes.text:
We call a nettle but a nettle, and
The faults of fools but folly.
quotes.plain: Call a thing what it is. A nuisance is a nuisance and a mistake is a mistake.

quotes.text:
I had rather be their servant in my way
Than sway with them in theirs.
quotes.plain: Better to serve on your own terms than to rule on someone else's.

quotes.text:
I had rather have my wounds to heal again
Than hear say how I got them.
quotes.plain: Do the work and skip the applause. Praise hurts more than the scars.

quotes.text:
I had rather have one scratch my head i’ th’ sun
When the alarum were struck than idly sit
To hear my nothings monstered.
quotes.plain: Better to be in the fight than to sit and listen to people inflate what you have done.

quotes.text: What is the city but the people?
quotes.plain: A place, a company, a country is only the people in it.

quotes.text:
But now ’tis odds beyond arithmetic,
And manhood is called foolery when it stands
Against a falling fabric.
quotes.plain: Some fights are lost already. Standing alone against a collapse is not courage.

quotes.text:
His nature is too noble for the world.
He would not flatter Neptune for his trident
Or Jove for’s power to thunder. His heart’s his mouth;
What his breast forges, that his tongue must vent,
And, being angry, does forget that ever
He heard the name of death.
quotes.plain: Honest to a fault. He will not flatter anyone and cannot hide his anger, and it costs him.

quotes.text:
I have a heart as little apt as yours,
But yet a brain that leads my use of anger
To better vantage.
quotes.plain: Same anger as you. I just aim it where it helps me.

quotes.text:
I will not do’t,
Lest I surcease to honour mine own truth
And, by my body’s action, teach my mind
A most inherent baseness.
quotes.plain: What you do with your body trains your mind. Act small and you become small.

quotes.text:
Despising
For you the city, thus I turn my back.
There is a world elsewhere.
quotes.plain: If this place does not want you, leave. The world is bigger than one room.

quotes.text:
You were used
To say extremities was the trier of spirits;
That common chances common men could bear;
That when the sea was calm, all boats alike
Showed mastership in floating; fortune’s blows
When most struck home, being gentle wounded craves
A noble cunning.
quotes.plain: Anyone can float in calm water. Hard blows test you, and taking them well takes skill.

quotes.text: I shall be loved when I am lacked.
quotes.plain: People only see what you were worth once you are gone.

quotes.text:
’Tis fond to wail inevitable strokes
As ’tis to laugh at ’em.
quotes.plain: It is foolish to cry over what cannot be avoided, and just as foolish to laugh it off.

quotes.text:
Now we have shown our power,
Let us seem humbler after it is done
Than when it was a-doing.
quotes.plain: After you win, act smaller than you did while you were fighting.

quotes.text:
Anger’s my meat. I sup upon myself
And so shall starve with feeding.
quotes.plain: Living on anger means eating yourself alive. It never fills you.

quotes.text:
Though thy tackle’s torn,
Thou show’st a noble vessel.
quotes.plain: Even broken and battered, you can still look like someone worth following.

quotes.text:
So our virtues
Lie in th’ interpretation of the time,
And power, unto itself most commendable,
Hath not a tomb so evident as a chair
T’ extol what it hath done.
quotes.plain: Your good name depends on the era judging it, and power's own praise is the loudest proof it is fading.

quotes.text:
One fire drives out one fire, one nail one nail;
Rights by rights falter; strengths by strengths do fail.
quotes.plain: A new force replaces an old one. Nothing holds just because it is strong now.

quotes.text:
He was not taken well; he had not dined.
The veins unfilled, our blood is cold, and then
We pout upon the morning, are unapt
To give or to forgive; but when we have stuffed
These pipes and these conveyances of our blood
With wine and feeding, we have suppler souls
Than in our priestlike fasts.
quotes.plain: A hungry, tired person is not at their best. Eat and rest before you judge or decide.

quotes.text:
Like a dull actor now,
I have forgot my part, and I am out,
Even to a full disgrace.
quotes.plain: The feeling of blanking in front of everyone. It happens to the best, and it passes.

quotes.text:
Think’st thou it honourable for a noble man
Still to remember wrongs?
quotes.plain: Holding on to every wrong done to you is not strength.

quotes.text: There is differency between a grub and a butterfly, yet your butterfly was a grub.
quotes.plain: People change completely. What you are now does not limit what you become.

quotes.text:
I am senseless of your wrath; a touch more rare
Subdues all pangs, all fears.
quotes.plain: When something matters more to you than the threat, the fear goes quiet.

quotes.text:
Blessed be those,
How mean soe’er, that have their honest wills,
Which seasons comfort.
quotes.plain: Lucky are the people with simple wants. Getting what you want is what makes comfort sweet.

quotes.text:
Boldness be my friend!
Arm me, audacity, from head to foot!
quotes.plain: Walking into something scary? Ask for nerve and put it on like armor.

quotes.text:
The cloyed will, That satiate yet unsatisfied desire, that tub
Both fill’d and running, ravening first the lamb,
Longs after for the garbage.
quotes.plain: A glutted appetite is never full. It eats the best and then craves the trash.

quotes.text:
Not any; but abide the change of time,
Quake in the present winter’s state, and wish
That warmer days would come.
quotes.plain: Some stretches you can only wait out. Shiver through the winter and keep wanting spring.

quotes.text:
I see before me, man. Nor here, nor here,
Nor what ensues, but have a fog in them
That I cannot look through.
quotes.plain: Nobody sees what's coming. Everything ahead is fog, so you move anyway.

quotes.text:
And often to our comfort shall we find
The sharded beetle in a safer hold
Than is the full-wing’d eagle.
quotes.plain: The small, quiet creature is often safer than the one flying highest. Height is exposure.

quotes.text:
Then was I as a tree
Whose boughs did bend with fruit. But in one night
A storm, or robbery, call it what you will,
Shook down my mellow hangings, nay, my leaves,
And left me bare to weather.
quotes.plain: You can be at the top and lose it all in one night. Favor is not something you own.

quotes.text:
No, ’tis slander,
Whose edge is sharper than the sword, whose tongue
Outvenoms all the worms of Nile, whose breath
Rides on the posting winds and doth belie
All corners of the world.
quotes.plain: A lie travels faster and cuts deeper than a blade.

quotes.text:
Hath Britain all the sun that shines? Day, night,
Are they not but in Britain? I’ th’ world’s volume
Our Britain seems as of it, but not in’t;
In a great pool a swan’s nest.
quotes.plain: Your small corner is not the world. There is more sun and more room out there.

quotes.text:
Yet famine,
Ere clean it o’erthrow nature, makes it valiant.
Plenty and peace breeds cowards; hardness ever
Of hardiness is mother.
quotes.plain: Comfort makes you soft. Hardship is what breeds the hard.

quotes.text:
The sweat of industry would dry and die
But for the end it works to.
quotes.plain: Hard work only feels worth it when you can see what it's for.

quotes.text:
Come, our stomachs
Will make what’s homely savoury; weariness
Can snore upon the flint, when resty sloth
Finds the down pillow hard.
quotes.plain: Work makes plain food taste great and a rock feel like a bed. Laziness finds even a pillow too hard.

quotes.text:
I know not why
I love this youth, and I have heard you say
Love’s reason’s without reason.
quotes.plain: Love doesn't come with a reason. You don't get to argue it into being.

quotes.text:
Those that I reverence, those I fear, the wise;
At fools I laugh, not fear them.
quotes.plain: Fear the wise. Don't give fools that much power over you.

quotes.text:
Thersites’ body is as good as Ajax’,
When neither are alive.
quotes.plain: The coward and the hero are equal once they're dead. Rank is temporary.

quotes.text:
Fear no more the heat o’ th’ sun,
Nor the furious winter’s rages;
Thou thy worldly task hast done,
Home art gone, and ta’en thy wages.
Golden lads and girls all must,
As chimney-sweepers, come to dust.
quotes.plain: Everyone ends up as dust, golden or not. So the weather of today can't be that big.
Kings, scholars and doctors all end the same. The powerful have no hold on the dead.

quotes.text:
The ground that gave them first has them again.
Their pleasures here are past, so is their pain.
quotes.plain: Pleasure and pain both end. The earth takes everyone back.

quotes.text:
Be cheerful; wipe thine eyes.
Some falls are means the happier to arise.
quotes.plain: Some falls set up the better rise. Wipe your face and keep going.

quotes.text:
All other doubts, by time let them be clear’d:
Fortune brings in some boats that are not steer’d.
quotes.plain: Time clears most doubts. And luck sometimes lands good things nobody steered.

quotes.text:
What pleasure, sir, find we in life, to lock it
From action and adventure?
quotes.plain: What's the point of a life you keep locked away from action?

quotes.text:
Let me make men know
More valour in me than my habits show.
quotes.plain: Don't let your clothes or your status say how much you have in you. Show it.

quotes.text:
To shame the guise o’ th’ world, I will begin
The fashion less without and more within.
quotes.plain: Care less about the outside and more about what's inside.
People who live off someone else's favor are dreaming. They wake up with nothing.
Real power over an enemy is the power to let them go.

quotes.text: A little more than kin, and less than kind.
quotes.plain: Related to him, but nothing like him in spirit.

quotes.text: Seems, madam! Nay, it is; I know not seems.
quotes.plain: I'm not performing grief. It's real. I don't do appearances.

quotes.text:
How weary, stale, flat, and unprofitable
Seem to me all the uses of this world!
quotes.plain: Some days everything looks gray and pointless. Hamlet felt it too, and wrote it down.

quotes.text:
He was a man, take him for all in all,
I shall not look upon his like again.
quotes.plain: Some people can't be replaced, and you only know it after they're gone.

quotes.text:
Be wary then, best safety lies in fear.
Youth to itself rebels, though none else near.
quotes.plain: Be careful. The young are their own worst enemy even with nobody around.

quotes.text:
And to my mind, though I am native here,
And to the manner born, it is a custom
More honour’d in the breach than the observance.
quotes.plain: Some habits are better broken than kept, however old they are.

quotes.text:
Why, what should be the fear?
I do not set my life at a pin’s fee;
And for my soul, what can it do to that,
Being a thing immortal as itself?
quotes.plain: Once you stop treating your life as precious, fear has nothing left to take.

quotes.text:
My fate cries out,
And makes each petty artery in this body
As hardy as the Nemean lion’s nerve.
quotes.plain: When you know what you're called to do, your body finds a strength it didn't have.

quotes.text: Something is rotten in the state of Denmark.
quotes.plain: Something at the top is wrong, and you can feel it before you can prove it.

quotes.text:
And duller shouldst thou be than the fat weed
That rots itself in ease on Lethe wharf,
Wouldst thou not stir in this.
quotes.plain: Anyone who stays comfortable when it matters is rotting.

quotes.text:
My tables. Meet it is I set it down,
That one may smile, and smile, and be a villain!
quotes.plain: A friendly face tells you nothing. Plenty of villains smile.

quotes.text:
And therefore as a stranger give it welcome.
There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio,
Than are dreamt of in your philosophy.
quotes.plain: Reality is bigger than your theory of it. Stay open.

quotes.text:
The time is out of joint. O cursed spite,
That ever I was born to set it right.
quotes.plain: The world is broken and somehow fixing it landed on you.

quotes.text:
My liege and madam, to expostulate
What majesty should be, what duty is,
Why day is day, night night, and time is time
Were nothing but to waste night, day and time.
Therefore, since brevity is the soul of wit,
And tediousness the limbs and outward flourishes,
I will be brief.
quotes.plain: Say it short. Long-windedness is just padding on a thin idea.

quotes.text: Ay sir, to be honest, as this world goes, is to be one man picked out of ten thousand.
quotes.plain: An honest person is rare. Be the one in ten thousand.

quotes.text:
Happy in that we are not over-happy;
On Fortune’s cap we are not the very button.
quotes.plain: Not at the very top and not at the bottom. That middle is a fine place to be.

quotes.text: Why, then ’tis none to you; for there is nothing either good or bad but thinking makes it so.
quotes.plain: Things aren't good or bad until your mind says so. Change the thought, change the weight.

quotes.text: O God, I could be bounded in a nutshell, and count myself a king of infinite space, were it not that I have bad dreams.
quotes.plain: A tiny life would be enough if your own mind would leave you alone.

quotes.text: What a piece of work is man, how noble in reason, how infinite in faculties, in form and moving, how express and admirable; in action how like an angel, in apprehension, how like a god: the beauty of the world, the paragon of animals. And yet, to me, what is this quintessence of dust?
quotes.plain: People are astonishing, and also just dust. Both are true and it can get you down.

quotes.text: Use every man after his desert, and who should ’scape whipping?
quotes.plain: If everyone got what they deserved, nobody would get off. Be generous.

quotes.text:
Yet I,
A dull and muddy-mettled rascal, peak
Like John-a-dreams, unpregnant of my cause,
And can say nothing.
quotes.plain: Watching someone else burn for nothing, while you drift with a real cause and do nothing.

quotes.text:
For murder, though it have no tongue, will speak
With most miraculous organ.
quotes.plain: Hidden wrongs come out eventually, one way or another.

quotes.text:
The play’s the thing
Wherein I’ll catch the conscience of the King.
quotes.plain: Stage the truth and see who flinches.

quotes.text:
’Tis too much prov’d, that with devotion’s visage
And pious action we do sugar o’er
The devil himself.
quotes.plain: A holy face and good deeds can cover up something rotten. We all do it.

quotes.text:
Thus conscience does make cowards of us all,
And thus the native hue of resolution
Is sicklied o’er with the pale cast of thought,
And enterprises of great pith and moment,
With this regard their currents turn awry
And lose the name of action.
quotes.plain: Overthinking kills big plans. The more you worry at a decision, the less you do it.

quotes.text: I am very proud, revengeful, ambitious, with more offences at my beck than I have thoughts to put them in, imagination to give them shape, or time to act them in. What should such fellows as I do crawling between earth and heaven?
quotes.plain: Hamlet's honest about his flaws. Naming your worst traits is where self-mastery starts.

quotes.text: Be thou as chaste as ice, as pure as snow, thou shalt not escape calumny.
quotes.plain: Be spotless and people will still talk. Live right and stop managing gossip.

quotes.text:
O, what a noble mind is here o’erthrown!
The courtier’s, soldier’s, scholar’s, eye, tongue, sword,
Th’expectancy and rose of the fair state,
The glass of fashion and the mould of form,
Th’observ’d of all observers, quite, quite down!
quotes.plain: Even the most promising mind can fall. Guard yours.

quotes.text: Be not too tame neither; but let your own discretion be your tutor.
quotes.plain: Rules only get you part of the way. Trust your own judgment for the rest.

quotes.text:
No, let the candied tongue lick absurd pomp,
And crook the pregnant hinges of the knee
Where thrift may follow fawning.
quotes.plain: Let others grovel for advantage. A real friend doesn't flatter you for a cut.

quotes.text:
And blessed are those
Whose blood and judgement are so well co-mingled
That they are not a pipe for Fortune’s finger
To sound what stop she please. Give me that man
That is not passion’s slave, and I will wear him
In my heart’s core, ay, in my heart of heart,
As I do thee.
quotes.plain: Be the person luck and mood can't play like an instrument. That's who earns real love.

quotes.text:
But what we do determine, oft we break.
Purpose is but the slave to memory,
Of violent birth, but poor validity:
Which now, like fruit unripe, sticks on the tree,
But fall unshaken when they mellow be.
quotes.plain: Resolutions are strong when made and weak a week later. Build the habit, not the mood.

quotes.text:
Most necessary ’tis that we forget
To pay ourselves what to ourselves is debt.
What to ourselves in passion we propose,
The passion ending, doth the purpose lose.
quotes.plain: We forget the promises we make ourselves. When the feeling fades, the plan goes with it.

quotes.text:
The great man down, you mark his favourite flies,
The poor advanc’d makes friends of enemies;
And hitherto doth love on fortune tend:
For who not needs shall never lack a friend,
And who in want a hollow friend doth try,
Directly seasons him his enemy.
quotes.plain: People stick around while you're winning and vanish when you fall. Test friends in hard times.

quotes.text:
Our wills and fates do so contrary run
That our devices still are overthrown.
Our thoughts are ours, their ends none of our own.
quotes.plain: You control your plans, not how they end. Make them anyway.

quotes.text: The lady protests too much, methinks.
quotes.plain: When someone defends too hard, something is off.

quotes.text: Why, let the strucken deer go weep, The hart ungalled play; For some must watch, while some must sleep, So runs the world away.
quotes.plain: Some people suffer while others play. That's how the world runs, so don't take it personally.

quotes.text: Call me what instrument you will, though you can fret me, you cannot play upon me.
quotes.plain: You can irritate me but you can't work me like a tool.

quotes.text:
My words fly up, my thoughts remain below.
Words without thoughts never to heaven go.
quotes.plain: Saying the right thing without meaning it gets you nowhere.

quotes.text: Assume a virtue, if you have it not.
quotes.plain: Act like the person you want to be before you are. The habit builds the person.

quotes.text:
Refrain tonight,
And that shall lend a kind of easiness
To the next abstinence. The next more easy;
For use almost can change the stamp of nature,
And either curb the devil, or throw him out
With wondrous potency.
quotes.plain: Say no tonight. Tomorrow's no is easier, and habit can rewrite your nature.

quotes.text:
I must be cruel, only to be kind:
Thus bad begins, and worse remains behind.
quotes.plain: Sometimes a hard thing now is the kind thing, and the worst is still ahead.

quotes.text: Your worm is your only emperor for diet. We fat all creatures else to fat us, and we fat ourselves for maggots. Your fat king and your lean beggar is but variable service, two dishes, but to one table. That’s the end.
quotes.plain: King and beggar both end up as worm food. Status doesn't survive death.

quotes.text:
Two thousand souls and twenty thousand ducats
Will not debate the question of this straw!
This is th’imposthume of much wealth and peace,
That inward breaks, and shows no cause without
Why the man dies.
quotes.plain: Armies fight over a patch of dirt that's worth nothing. Comfort breeds pointless quarrels.

quotes.text: Lord, we know what we are, but know not what we may be.
quotes.plain: You know who you are today. You have no idea who you could become.

quotes.text: My will, not all the world.
quotes.plain: The only thing that can stop you is your own will.

quotes.text:
That we would do,
We should do when we would; for this ‘would’ changes,
And hath abatements and delays as many
As there are tongues, are hands, are accidents;
And then this ‘should’ is like a spendthrift sigh
That hurts by easing.
quotes.plain: Do it when you want to do it. The wanting fades, delays pile up, and sighing about it doesn't help.

quotes.text:
One woe doth tread upon another’s heel,
So fast they follow.
quotes.plain: Bad things come in a line. Keep your footing.

quotes.text:
But age with his stealing steps
Hath claw’d me in his clutch,
And hath shipp’d me into the land,
As if I had never been such.
quotes.plain: Age sneaks up without a sound and then it's over, as if you were never there.

quotes.text: Is this the fine of his fines, and the recovery of his recoveries, to have his fine pate full of fine dirt?
quotes.plain: All that scheming over land, and the payoff is a head full of dirt.

quotes.text: Alas, poor Yorick. I knew him, Horatio, a fellow of infinite jest, of most excellent fancy.
quotes.plain: The funniest, liveliest person is a skull in the end. So laugh while you can.

quotes.text: Now get you to my lady’s chamber, and tell her, let her paint an inch thick, to this favour she must come.
quotes.plain: No amount of makeup stops the skull showing. Don't spend your life on appearances.

quotes.text: To what base uses we may return, Horatio! Why may not imagination trace the noble dust of Alexander till he find it stopping a bung-hole?
quotes.plain: Even the greatest conqueror ends up as dirt plugging a barrel. Ambition is humbled by the grave.

quotes.text: Imperious Caesar, dead and turn’d to clay, Might stop a hole to keep the wind away. O, that that earth which kept the world in awe Should patch a wall t’expel the winter’s flaw.
quotes.plain: The man who ruled the world now fills a crack in a wall. All power ends here.

quotes.text: Sweets to the sweet. Farewell.
quotes.plain: A tender goodbye, flowers for the dead.

quotes.text:
Let Hercules himself do what he may,
The cat will mew, and dog will have his day.
quotes.plain: Even the strongest can't stop the world from running its course. Everyone gets their day.

quotes.text:
Our indiscretion sometime serves us well,
When our deep plots do pall; and that should teach us
There’s a divinity that shapes our ends,
Rough-hew them how we will.
quotes.plain: Sometimes the plan fails and the reckless move works. Something bigger shapes the result, however you carve it.

quotes.text:
It will be short. The interim is mine;
And a man’s life’s no more than to say ‘One’.
quotes.plain: The time between now and the end is yours to use. And a life is as quick as counting one.

quotes.text: Not a whit, we defy augury. There’s a special providence in the fall of a sparrow. If it be now, ’tis not to come; if it be not to come, it will be now; if it be not now, yet it will come. The readiness is all.
quotes.plain: You can't dodge what's coming or predict it. Be ready, and that's enough.

quotes.text:
Why, as a woodcock to my own springe, Osric.
I am justly kill’d with mine own treachery.
quotes.plain: He walked into his own trap. Schemes against others come back to you.

quotes.text:
O good Horatio, what a wounded name,
Things standing thus unknown, shall live behind me.
quotes.plain: What people believe about you will outlive you, so make sure someone knows the truth.

quotes.text: The rest is silence.
quotes.plain: In the end there's nothing more to say. Say what matters now.

quotes.text:
Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince,
And flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.
quotes.plain: A good friend's farewell. Say it the way you'd want it said to you.

quotes.text:
The edge of war, like an ill-sheathed knife,
No more shall cut his master.
quotes.plain: Violence you can't control ends up cutting you.

quotes.text: Thou didst well, for wisdom cries out in the streets and no man regards it.
quotes.plain: Good advice is everywhere and almost nobody listens.

quotes.text:
If all the year were playing holidays,
To sport would be as tedious as to work;
But, when they seldom come, they wish’d-for come,
And nothing pleaseth but rare accidents.
quotes.plain: Rest feels good because work is the rule. Endless fun turns boring.

quotes.text:
And, like bright metal on a sullen ground,
My reformation, glitt’ring o’er my fault,
Shall show more goodly and attract more eyes
Than that which hath no foil to set it off.
quotes.plain: A comeback shines brightest against a bad past. Your low point makes the rise look better.

quotes.text:
I’ll so offend, to make offence a skill,
Redeeming time, when men think least I will.
quotes.plain: Let them underestimate you, then turn it around when they least expect it.

quotes.text:
If we fall in, good night, or sink or swim!
Send danger from the east unto the west,
So honour cross it from the north to south,
And let them grapple. O, the blood more stirs
To rouse a lion than to start a hare!
quotes.plain: Go for the big danger. A lion wakes your blood. A hare doesn't.

quotes.text:
By Heaven, methinks it were an easy leap
To pluck bright honour from the pale-faced moon,
Or dive into the bottom of the deep,
Where fathom-line could never touch the ground,
And pluck up drowned honour by the locks,
So he that doth redeem her thence might wear
Without corrival all her dignities.
quotes.plain: When your sights are set high enough, even impossible leaps feel easy. Ambition at full blast.

quotes.text: ’Tis dangerous to take a cold, to sleep, to drink; but I tell you, my lord fool, out of this nettle, danger, we pluck this flower, safety.
quotes.plain: Everything has risk. Grab the nettle and you get the flower.

quotes.text: Banish plump Jack, and banish all the world.
quotes.plain: Cut out the one who brings the joy and you've cut out the world.

quotes.text:
Why, so can I, or so can any man,
But will they come when you do call for them?
quotes.plain: Anyone can claim big powers. The proof is whether it works when called.

quotes.text:
And I can teach thee, coz, to shame the devil
By telling truth; tell truth, and shame the devil.
quotes.plain: Telling the truth beats the devil at his own game.

quotes.text:
By being seldom seen, I could not stir
But like a comet I was wonder’d at,
That men would tell their children, “This is he.”
quotes.plain: Don't be everywhere. Rare appearances make people take notice.

quotes.text:
Our hands are full of business. Let’s away,
Advantage feeds him fat while men delay.
quotes.plain: Delay feeds your opponent. Move now.

quotes.text: Company, villainous company, hath been the spoil of me.
quotes.plain: The people you run with are what ruin you.

quotes.text: Honour is a mere scutcheon. And so ends my catechism.
quotes.plain: Reputation is a painted shield. The dead don't feel it and the living won't keep it.

quotes.text:
O gentlemen, the time of life is short!
To spend that shortness basely were too long
If life did ride upon a dial’s point,
Still ending at the arrival of an hour.
quotes.plain: Life is short, so spending it small and cheap is a waste even if you only had an hour.

quotes.text:
Two stars keep not their motion in one sphere,
Nor can one England brook a double reign,
Of Harry Percy and the Prince of Wales.
quotes.plain: Two people can't both be number one in the same place.
Losing to a rival hurts the pride more than any wound hurts the body.

quotes.text:
But thoughts, the slaves of life, and life, time’s fool,
And time, that takes survey of all the world,
Must have a stop.
quotes.plain: Your thoughts serve your life, your life serves time, and time ends for everything.

quotes.text:
Ill-weaved ambition, how much art thou shrunk!
When that this body did contain a spirit,
A kingdom for it was too small a bound;
But now two paces of the vilest earth
Is room enough.
quotes.plain: The man who thought a kingdom was too small now needs two paces of dirt.

quotes.text: The better part of valour is discretion, in the which better part I have saved my life.
quotes.plain: Knowing when to back off is half of courage. Falstaff just uses it as an excuse.

quotes.text:
Yet the first bringer of unwelcome news
Hath but a losing office, and his tongue
Sounds ever after as a sullen bell,
Remember’d tolling a departing friend.
quotes.plain: Whoever brings bad news gets hated for it, like a bell that tolls a death.
You knew the odds were bad when you went in. Capsized, you go out again.

quotes.text: I can get no remedy against this consumption of the purse. Borrowing only lingers and lingers it out, but the disease is incurable.
quotes.plain: Borrowing doesn't cure being broke. It only drags the sickness out.

quotes.text: A good wit will make use of anything. I will turn diseases to commodity.
quotes.plain: A sharp mind finds a way to use even its own bad luck.

quotes.text:
When we mean to build,
We first survey the plot, then draw the model,
And when we see the figure of the house,
Then we must rate the cost of the erection,
Which if we find outweighs ability,
What do we then but draw anew the model
In fewer offices, or at least desist
To build at all?
quotes.plain: Count the cost before you build, and shrink the plan if you can't afford it.

quotes.text:
An habitation giddy and unsure
Hath he that buildeth on the vulgar heart.
quotes.plain: Build on the crowd's love and you're building on sand.

quotes.text:
O thoughts of men accursed!
Past and to come seems best; things present, worst.
quotes.plain: People always praise the past and the future and complain about right now.

quotes.text: We are time’s subjects, and time bids be gone.
quotes.plain: Time is the boss and it says move.

quotes.text: Let the end try the man.
quotes.plain: Judge me by how it all ends, not by how it looks now.

quotes.text: Well, thus we play the fools with the time, and the spirits of the wise sit in the clouds and mock us.
quotes.plain: We waste our days acting the fool while wiser people look down and laugh.

quotes.text: Peace, good Doll, do not speak like a death’s-head; do not bid me remember mine end.
quotes.plain: Nobody wants the reminder that they're going to die, which is why they need it.

quotes.text: Is it not strange that desire should so many years outlive performance?
quotes.plain: The wanting outlasts the ability to do anything about it.

quotes.text:
By heaven, Poins, I feel me much to blame,
So idly to profane the precious time,
When tempest of commotion, like the south
Borne with black vapour, doth begin to melt
And drop upon our bare unarmed heads.
quotes.plain: The storm is about to break and you're out here wasting precious time.

quotes.text:
There is a history in all men’s lives
Figuring the natures of the times deceased;
The which observed, a man may prophesy,
With a near aim, of the main chance of things
As yet not come to life, who in their seeds
And weak beginning lie intreasured.
quotes.plain: Study the past and you can predict what's coming, because everything starts as a small seed.

quotes.text:
Are these things then necessities?
Then let us meet them like necessities;
quotes.plain: If it can't be avoided, face it like something that can't be avoided.

quotes.text: Certain, ’tis certain, very sure, very sure. Death, as the Psalmist saith, is certain to all, all shall die.
quotes.plain: Death is certain for everyone, so what are you saving yourself for?

quotes.text: We have heard the chimes at midnight, Master Shallow.
quotes.plain: We have had our wild nights and they are gone.

quotes.text: A man can die but once. We owe God a death.
quotes.plain: You only die once and it's already owed, so don't live like a coward.

quotes.text: Care I for the limb, the thews, the stature, bulk, and big assemblance of a man? Give me the spirit, Master Shallow.
quotes.plain: Size and muscle mean little. Pick the person with spirit.
A real peace is a win for both sides because nobody has to lose.

quotes.text:
Will Fortune never come with both hands full,
But write her fair words still in foulest letters?
She either gives a stomach and no food, Such are the poor, in health; or else a feast
And takes away the stomach, such are the rich,
That have abundance and enjoy it not.
quotes.plain: Luck gives you the appetite or the meal, never both. The poor are hungry, the rich can't enjoy it.

quotes.text: Thy wish was father, Harry, to that thought.
quotes.plain: You believed it because you wanted it to be true.

quotes.text: Thou seek’st the greatness that will overwhelm thee.
quotes.plain: The big thing you chase may be the thing that crushes you.

quotes.text:
This new and gorgeous garment, majesty,
Sits not so easy on me as you think.
quotes.plain: Power looks comfortable from outside and weighs a lot from inside.

quotes.text:
The tide of blood in me
Hath proudly flow’d in vanity till now.
Now doth it turn and ebb back to the sea,
Where it shall mingle with the state of floods,
And flow henceforth in formal majesty.
quotes.plain: The wild years are over. From here on I run on discipline.

quotes.text: O God, that right should thus overcome might! Well, of sufferance comes ease.
quotes.plain: Enduring a thing is how it eventually gets easier.

quotes.text:
I know thee not, old man. Fall to thy prayers.
How ill white hairs becomes a fool and jester!
quotes.plain: Once you outgrow the people who kept you small, you stop pretending you know them.
The life you drifted through looks ugly once you wake up.
Cut the excess and build some character. Indulgence digs your grave faster.
Don't treat me like who I used to be. I dropped that self and the crowd that came with it.

quotes.text:
O for a Muse of fire, that would ascend
The brightest heaven of invention,
A kingdom for a stage, princes to act,
And monarchs to behold the swelling scene!
quotes.plain: Give me a fire big enough for the story I'm trying to tell.

quotes.text: Piece out our imperfections with your thoughts.
quotes.plain: What you lack in means, your mind can make up.

quotes.text:
The strawberry grows underneath the nettle,
And wholesome berries thrive and ripen best
Neighboured by fruit of baser quality;
And so the Prince obscured his contemplation
Under the veil of wildness, which, no doubt,
Grew like the summer grass, fastest by night,
Unseen, yet crescive in his faculty.
quotes.plain: Growth often happens unseen, in bad company, while everyone thinks you're wasting time.
Many separate efforts can all land on one target if the aim is clear.

quotes.text: Though patience be a tired mare, yet she will plod.
quotes.plain: Patience may be worn out, but she keeps walking.

quotes.text: ’A parted even just between twelve and one, even at the turning o’ the tide: for after I saw him fumble with the sheets, and play with flowers, and smile upon his fingers’ ends, I knew there was but one way; for his nose was as sharp as a pen, and ’a babbled of green fields.
quotes.plain: Even the loudest life ends quietly, with a man talking about green fields.
Promises are cheap and people are flimsy. Be careful who you count on.

quotes.text:
Self-love, my liege, is not so vile a sin
As self-neglecting.
quotes.plain: Thinking well of yourself is better than letting yourself go.

quotes.text:
Now he weighs time
Even to the utmost grain.
quotes.plain: He treats every grain of time as if it were worth something.

quotes.text:
Once more unto the breach, dear friends, once more,
Or close the wall up with our English dead.
quotes.plain: Go at it one more time, or watch it all fall in.
Be humble when it's calm. When it gets hard, stiffen up and go in like a tiger.

quotes.text:
I see you stand like greyhounds in the slips,
Straining upon the start. The game’s afoot!
Follow your spirit, and upon this charge
Cry, “God for Harry! England and Saint George!”
quotes.plain: You're straining at the start already. Follow that drive.

quotes.text: Would I were in an alehouse in London! I would give all my fame for a pot of ale and safety.
quotes.plain: Everyone wants to trade the glory for safety when fear sets in.

quotes.text: Fortune is painted blind, with a muffler afore his eyes, to signify to you that Fortune is blind; and she is painted also with a wheel, to signify to you, which is the moral of it, that she is turning, and inconstant, and mutability, and variation; and her foot, look you, is fixed upon a spherical stone, which rolls, and rolls, and rolls.
quotes.plain: Luck is blind and always turning, so neither the good nor the bad times last.

quotes.text:
We would not seek a battle, as we are;
Nor, as we are, we say we will not shun it.
quotes.plain: Don't go looking for the fight, and don't run from it either.

quotes.text: We are in God’s hands, brother, not in theirs.
quotes.plain: What happens to you isn't up to them. Stay steady.

quotes.text:
Upon his royal face there is no note
How dread an army hath enrounded him;
Nor doth he dedicate one jot of colour
Unto the weary and all-watched night,
But freshly looks, and over-bears attaint
With cheerful semblance and sweet majesty;
That every wretch, pining and pale before,
Beholding him, plucks comfort from his looks.
quotes.plain: Show calm on your face when you're surrounded and the people around you will borrow it.

quotes.text:
A largess universal like the sun
His liberal eye doth give to everyone,
Thawing cold fear, that mean and gentle all
Behold, as may unworthiness define,
A little touch of Harry in the night.
quotes.plain: A leader who stays warm and steady in the dark melts everyone else's fear.

quotes.text:
Gloucester, ’tis true that we are in great danger;
The greater therefore should our courage be.
quotes.plain: The bigger the danger, the bigger your courage has to be.

quotes.text:
There is some soul of goodness in things evil,
Would men observingly distil it out;
quotes.plain: Even bad things hold something useful if you look closely.

quotes.text:
Thus may we gather honey from the weed,
And make a moral of the devil himself.
quotes.plain: You can pull something sweet out of whatever's bothering you.

quotes.text: We see yonder the beginning of the day, but I think we shall never see the end of it.
quotes.plain: Dread says the day is going to break you before it ends.

quotes.text: His ceremonies laid by, in his nakedness he appears but a man; and though his affections are higher mounted than ours, yet, when they stoop, they stoop with the like wing.
quotes.plain: Strip off the title and a king is just a man with the same fears as you.

quotes.text: Every subject’s duty is the King’s; but every subject’s soul is his own.
quotes.plain: You can owe someone your work. You still own your conscience.

quotes.text:
O God of battles! steel my soldiers’ hearts.
Possess them not with fear.
quotes.plain: Make us hard and keep fear out.

quotes.text:
If we are mark’d to die, we are enough
To do our country loss; and if to live,
The fewer men, the greater share of honour.
quotes.plain: Small numbers don't matter. If you win, fewer people share the credit.

quotes.text:
We would not die in that man’s company
That fears his fellowship to die with us.
quotes.plain: Don't take anyone who's afraid to stand with you.

quotes.text:
Old men forget; yet all shall be forgot,
But he’ll remember with advantages
What feats he did that day.
quotes.plain: Everything gets forgotten in time, and people still polish their best days.

quotes.text:
We few, we happy few, we band of brothers.
For he today that sheds his blood with me
Shall be my brother; be he ne’er so vile,
This day shall gentle his condition;
quotes.plain: Fighting side by side makes you family, whatever you were before.

quotes.text: All things are ready, if our minds be so.
quotes.plain: The only thing left is whether your mind is ready.

quotes.text:
Let me speak proudly: tell the Constable
We are but warriors for the working-day.
quotes.plain: We're not here to look good. We're here to work.

quotes.text: A good leg will fall; a straight back will stoop; a black beard will turn white; a curl’d pate will grow bald; a fair face will wither; a full eye will wax hollow; but a good heart, Kate, is the sun and the moon; or rather the sun and not the moon; for it shines bright and never changes, but keeps his course truly.
quotes.plain: Looks and strength fade. A steady heart is the only thing that lasts.

quotes.text:
Small time, but in that small most greatly lived
This star of England.
quotes.plain: He had little time and used every bit of it.

quotes.text:
Awake, awake, English nobility!
Let not sloth dim your honours new-begot.
quotes.plain: Wake up. Laziness will dim what you just earned.

quotes.text:
Glory is like a circle in the water,
Which never ceaseth to enlarge itself
Till by broad spreading it disperse to nought.
quotes.plain: Glory spreads out like a ripple and then disappears. Nothing you win stays big on its own.

quotes.text:
And here I prophesy: this brawl today,
Grown to this faction in the Temple Garden,
Shall send between the Red Rose and the White
A thousand souls to death and deadly night.
quotes.plain: One petty argument today turns into a war that kills thousands. Small grudges grow.

quotes.text:
Believe me, lords, my tender years can tell
Civil dissension is a viperous worm
That gnaws the bowels of the commonwealth.
quotes.plain: Infighting is a worm that eats a group from the inside.

quotes.text: Defer no time, delays have dangerous ends;
quotes.plain: Delay is dangerous. Move now.

quotes.text:
Care is no cure, but rather corrosive,
For things that are not to be remedied.
quotes.plain: Worrying fixes nothing and eats at you. Don't brood over what can't be changed.

quotes.text:
Good Lord, what madness rules in brainsick men,
When for so slight and frivolous a cause
Such factious emulations shall arise!
quotes.plain: People tear things apart over trivial causes, and it is madness.
When the weak hold power it is bad, and when envy splits the people it is worse. That is where ruin starts.

quotes.text:
If we be English deer, be then in blood;
Not rascal-like, to fall down with a pinch,
But rather, moody-mad and desperate stags,
Turn on the bloody hounds with heads of steel
And make the cowards stand aloof at bay.
quotes.plain: If you are going to be hunted, turn on the hounds. Don't fall down at the first pinch.

quotes.text:
Sell every man his life as dear as mine,
And they shall find dear deer of us, my friends.
quotes.plain: If you have to go down, make them pay full price.

quotes.text: His fame lives in the world, his shame in you.
quotes.plain: Your reputation outlives you, and so does your shame.

quotes.text:
There is no hope that ever I will stay
If the first hour I shrink and run away.
quotes.plain: If I run the first time I'm scared, I'll never stop running.

quotes.text:
If I today die not with Frenchmen’s rage,
Tomorrow I shall die with mickle age.
quotes.plain: If I don't die today, I die tomorrow anyway. One more day is a small thing to risk.

quotes.text:
Triumphant Death, smear’d with captivity,
Young Talbot’s valour makes me smile at thee.
quotes.plain: Death does not scare a man who has seen his son's courage. He can smile at it.

quotes.text:
Thou antic Death, which laugh’st us here to scorn,
Anon, from thy insulting tyranny,
Coupled in bonds of perpetuity,
Two Talbots, winged through the lither sky,
In thy despite shall scape mortality.
quotes.plain: Death mocks us now, but what we do can outlast it.

quotes.text: Of all base passions, fear is most accursed.
quotes.plain: Of all the base feelings, fear is the worst.

quotes.text: Pride went before; Ambition follows him.
quotes.plain: Pride clears the road and ambition walks in behind it.

quotes.text: A day will come when York shall claim his own;
quotes.plain: A day will come when I take what is mine.

quotes.text: Then, York, be still awhile till time do serve.
quotes.plain: Stay quiet and wait until the time is right.

quotes.text:
My lord, ’tis but a base ignoble mind
That mounts no higher than a bird can soar.
quotes.plain: It is a small mind that never reaches higher than a bird can fly.

quotes.text:
Thus sometimes hath the brightest day a cloud,
And after summer evermore succeeds
Barren winter, with his wrathful nipping cold;
So cares and joys abound, as seasons fleet.
quotes.plain: Even the brightest day gets a cloud, and winter follows summer. Cares and joys come and go like seasons.
Pull weeds while they're shallow. Let them grow and they choke the garden.

quotes.text:
Smooth runs the water where the brook is deep,
And in his simple show he harbours treason.
The fox barks not when he would steal the lamb.
quotes.plain: The quiet ones with the smooth surface may be the ones plotting. Watch the still water.

quotes.text:
Thus are my blossoms blasted in the bud,
And caterpillars eat my leaves away;
But I will remedy this gear ere long,
Or sell my title for a glorious grave.
quotes.plain: My hopes were killed in the bud, but I'll fix it soon or die trying.

quotes.text:
A heart unspotted is not easily daunted.
The purest spring is not so free from mud
As I am clear from treason to my sovereign.
quotes.plain: A clean conscience is not easily scared. I am as free of guilt as the purest spring is of mud.

quotes.text:
Virtue is choked with foul ambition,
And charity chased hence by rancour’s hand;
quotes.plain: Ambition chokes virtue, and bitterness chases away kindness.

quotes.text:
Show me one scar charactered on thy skin;
Men’s flesh preserved so whole do seldom win.
quotes.plain: If you haven't been scarred, you haven't won anything.

quotes.text:
Now, York, or never, steel thy fearful thoughts,
And change misdoubt to resolution.
quotes.plain: Now or never. Steel your nerve and turn doubt into resolve.

quotes.text:
What stronger breastplate than a heart untainted?
Thrice is he armed that hath his quarrel just,
And he but naked, though locked up in steel,
Whose conscience with injustice is corrupted.
quotes.plain: Nothing armors you like a clear conscience. A just cause makes you strong, and a corrupt one leaves you exposed.
With you, a wilderness is full of people. Without you, the whole world is empty.

quotes.text:
If thou be’st Death, I’ll give thee England’s treasure,
Enough to purchase such another island,
So thou wilt let me live and feel no pain.
quotes.plain: Money can't buy off death, and a dying man would pay anything to live.

quotes.text: So bad a death argues a monstrous life.
quotes.plain: The way someone dies shows how they lived.

quotes.text: Forbear to judge, for we are sinners all.
quotes.plain: Don't judge. Everyone has failed somewhere.

quotes.text: Small things make base men proud.
quotes.plain: Petty people puff up over petty wins.

quotes.text:
True nobility is exempt from fear;
More can I bear than you dare execute.
quotes.plain: Real nobility doesn't flinch. I can take more than you can dish out.

quotes.text: The first thing we do, let’s kill all the lawyers.
quotes.plain: A mob always starts by removing the people who understand the rules.

quotes.text: Some say the bee stings, but I say ’tis the bee’s wax; for I did but seal once to a thing, and I was never mine own man since.
quotes.plain: Be careful what you sign. One signature and you are never your own man again.

quotes.text: Trust nobody, for fear you be betrayed.
quotes.plain: Trust nobody, or you'll get betrayed.

quotes.text:
The trust I have is in mine innocence,
And therefore am I bold and resolute.
quotes.plain: Innocence gives you nerve. If you've done nothing wrong you can stand firm.

quotes.text:
And seeing ignorance is the curse of God,
Knowledge the wing wherewith we fly to heaven,
Unless you be possessed with devilish spirits,
You cannot but forbear to murder me.
quotes.plain: Ignorance is a curse, and knowledge is the wing we fly on.

quotes.text:
Great men have reaching hands; oft have I struck
Those that I never saw, and struck them dead.
quotes.plain: Powerful people reach farther than they can see. Their decisions land on strangers.

quotes.text:
Was never subject longed to be a king
As I do long and wish to be a subject.
quotes.plain: No subject ever wanted to be a king as much as I want to be a subject. The crown costs peace.

quotes.text:
Lord, who would live turmoiled in the court
And may enjoy such quiet walks as these?
This small inheritance my father left me
Contenteth me, and worth a monarchy.
quotes.plain: Why live in turmoil at court when a small, quiet life is worth a monarchy?

quotes.text:
I seek not to wax great by others’ waning,
Or gather wealth, I care not with what envy;
Sufficeth that I have maintains my state
And sends the poor well pleased from my gate.
quotes.plain: I don't want to rise by someone else's fall. What I have is enough, and I share it.

quotes.text: Let them obey that knows not how to rule.
quotes.plain: If you can't lead, follow.

quotes.text:
It is great sin to swear unto a sin,
But greater sin to keep a sinful oath.
quotes.plain: Breaking a bad promise is better than keeping it.

quotes.text:
Fear frames disorder, and disorder wounds
Where it should guard.
quotes.plain: Fear leads to disorder, and disorder hurts you right where you needed to be protected.

quotes.text: But thou prefer’st thy life before thine honour.
quotes.plain: You chose your life over your honour.

quotes.text:
And, father, do but think
How sweet a thing it is to wear a crown,
Within whose circuit is Elysium
And all that poets feign of bliss and joy.
quotes.plain: Think how sweet it is to wear the crown, with every bliss poets ever imagined inside it.

quotes.text:
Unless the adage must be verified,
That beggars mounted run their horse to death.
quotes.plain: Beggars on horseback ride the horse to death.

quotes.text: Now my soul’s palace is become a prison.
quotes.plain: Your own mind can turn into the cell you can't leave.

quotes.text:
Stay we no longer dreaming of renown,
But sound the trumpets and about our task.
quotes.plain: Stop dreaming of glory and get to the task.

quotes.text:
The smallest worm will turn, being trodden on,
And doves will peck in safeguard of their brood.
quotes.plain: Even the smallest worm turns when trodden on.

quotes.text:
But, Clifford, tell me, didst thou never hear
That things ill got had ever bad success?
quotes.plain: Things gotten the wrong way never end well.

quotes.text:
I’ll leave my son my virtuous deeds behind,
And would my father had left me no more;
For all the rest is held at such a rate
As brings a thousand-fold more care to keep
Than in possession any jot of pleasure.
quotes.plain: I'd leave my son my good deeds and nothing more. All the rest costs more care to keep than it gives in pleasure.

quotes.text:
So minutes, hours, days, months, and years,
Passed over to the end they were created,
Would bring white hairs unto a quiet grave.
quotes.plain: Minutes, hours, days, months and years pass, and a simple life ends at a quiet grave with white hair.

quotes.text:
Gives not the hawthorn bush a sweeter shade
To shepherds looking on their silly sheep
Than doth a rich embroidered canopy
To kings that fear their subjects’ treachery?
quotes.plain: A hawthorn shade feels better to a shepherd than a canopy does to a king who fears his own people.

quotes.text: Ill blows the wind that profits nobody.
quotes.plain: It's an ill wind that blows no one any good.

quotes.text:
Whiles lions war and battle for their dens,
Poor harmless lambs abide their enmity.
quotes.plain: When the strong fight for territory, the harmless pay for it.

quotes.text:
Let me embrace thee, sour adversity,
For wise men say it is the wisest course.
quotes.plain: Welcome adversity. Wise people say it is the wisest teacher.
My crown is in my heart, not on my head. It is called contentment, and kings rarely have it.

quotes.text:
For many men that stumble at the threshold
Are well foretold that danger lurks within.
quotes.plain: Hesitation at the door is often your instinct warning you. Listen to it.

quotes.text: And fearless minds climb soonest unto crowns.
quotes.plain: Nerve gets you to the top before talent does.

quotes.text:
A little fire is quickly trodden out,
Which, being suffered, rivers cannot quench.
quotes.plain: Stamp out a small fire now, or no river will put it out later.

quotes.text: The harder matched, the greater victory.
quotes.plain: The harder the opponent, the bigger the win.

quotes.text:
Lo, now my glory smeared in dust and blood!
My parks, my walks, my manors that I had,
Even now forsake me; and of all my lands
Is nothing left me but my body’s length.
Why, what is pomp, rule, reign, but earth and dust?
And live we how we can, yet die we must.
quotes.plain: Power, land, and fame end as dust. You get to choose how you live, not whether you die.

quotes.text:
Great lords, wise men ne’er sit and wail their loss,
But cheerly seek how to redress their harms.
quotes.plain: Smart people skip the wailing and start fixing.

quotes.text: As good to chide the waves as speak them fair.
quotes.plain: Complaining to the waves changes nothing. Neither does asking nicely.

quotes.text:
Why, courage then! What cannot be avoided
’Twere childish weakness to lament or fear.
quotes.plain: What you can't avoid, you don't get to dread. Spend that energy on something else.

quotes.text:
Suspicion always haunts the guilty mind;
The thief doth fear each bush an officer.
quotes.plain: A guilty mind sees danger everywhere.

quotes.text:
This shoulder was ordained so thick to heave,
And heave it shall some weight or break my back.
quotes.plain: I'll carry the weight or break trying.

quotes.text:
To climb steep hills
Requires slow pace at first. Anger is like
A full hot horse, who being allowed his way,
Self-mettle tires him.
quotes.plain: Rushing and rage burn you out before you arrive. Anger wears out its own rider.

quotes.text:
Heat not a furnace for your foe so hot
That it do singe yourself. We may outrun
By violent swiftness that which we run at,
And lose by over-running.
quotes.plain: Make your enemy's fire too hot and you get burned. Too much speed loses the race.

quotes.text:
’Tis but the fate of place, and the rough brake
That virtue must go through.
quotes.plain: Being misjudged is the price of standing out.

quotes.text:
For our best act. If we shall stand still
In fear our motion will be mocked or carped at,
We should take root here where we sit,
Or sit state-statues only.
quotes.plain: Fear of criticism will root you in place like a statue.

quotes.text:
Things done well,
And with a care, exempt themselves from fear;
Things done without example, in their issue
Are to be feared.
quotes.plain: Done right and openly, there's nothing to fear. Done in the dark, expect trouble.

quotes.text:
When I came hither, I was Lord High Constable
And Duke of Buckingham; now, poor Edward Bohun.
quotes.plain: Titles go. Stripped of them, you are just who you were.

quotes.text:
Where you are liberal of your loves and counsels
Be sure you be not loose; for those you make friends
And give your hearts to, when they once perceive
The least rub in your fortunes, fall away
Like water from ye, never found again
But where they mean to sink ye.
quotes.plain: Be careful who you hand your heart to. Some friends vanish at the first crack in your luck.

quotes.text:
Farewell. And when you would say something that is sad,
Speak how I fell.
quotes.plain: If you must talk about my failure, tell it straight.

quotes.text:
Verily,
I swear, ’tis better to be lowly born
And range with humble livers in content
Than to be perked up in a glist’ring grief,
And wear a golden sorrow.
quotes.plain: Better to be humble and content than glittering and miserable.

quotes.text:
Our content
Is our best having.
quotes.plain: What you have, and being fine with it, is the best thing you own.

quotes.text: Out with it boldly. Truth loves open dealing.
quotes.plain: Say it plainly. The truth does not hide.

quotes.text:
Heaven is above all yet; there sits a judge
That no king can corrupt.
quotes.plain: No power on earth can bribe the final judge.

quotes.text:
I have touched the highest point of all my greatness,
And from that full meridian of my glory
I haste now to my setting. I shall fall
Like a bright exhalation in the evening,
And no man see me more.
quotes.plain: I peaked, and now I set like the sun. No one will see me again.

quotes.text: Press not a falling man too far! ’Tis virtue.
quotes.plain: Don't kick someone who's already down.

quotes.text:
This is the state of man: today he puts forth
The tender leaves of hopes; tomorrow blossoms,
And bears his blushing honours thick upon him;
The third day comes a frost, a killing frost,
And when he thinks, good easy man, full surely
His greatness is a-ripening, nips his root,
And then he falls, as I do.
quotes.plain: Hope blooms, honor piles up, then one frost kills the root. Greatness is never as safe as it feels.

quotes.text:
I have ventured,
Like little wanton boys that swim on bladders,
This many summers in a sea of glory,
But far beyond my depth.
quotes.plain: I swam in a sea of glory far past what I could handle.

quotes.text:
Vain pomp and glory of this world, I hate ye!
I feel my heart new opened. O, how wretched
Is that poor man that hangs on princes’ favours!
quotes.plain: Chasing a prince's favor is a miserable way to live.

quotes.text:
Never so truly happy, my good Cromwell.
I know myself now, and I feel within me
A peace above all earthly dignities,
A still and quiet conscience.
quotes.plain: Losing everything, he finally knows himself, and feels peace.

quotes.text:
Mark but my fall and that that ruined me.
Cromwell, I charge thee, fling away ambition!
By that sin fell the angels; how can man, then,
The image of his maker, hope to win by it?
Love thyself last; cherish those hearts that hate thee.
Corruption wins not more than honesty.
quotes.plain: Ambition ruined the angels. Honesty beats corruption in the end.

quotes.text:
Be just, and fear not.
Let all the ends thou aim’st at be thy country’s,
Thy God’s, and truth’s.
quotes.plain: Be fair, drop the fear, and aim at something bigger than yourself.

quotes.text:
Had I but served my God with half the zeal
I served my king, He would not in mine age
Have left me naked to mine enemies.
quotes.plain: Give your God the zeal you give your boss, or you'll be left naked when the boss drops you.

quotes.text:
Men’s evil manners live in brass; their virtues
We write in water.
quotes.plain: People remember your faults for good and your virtues for a day.

quotes.text:
His overthrow heaped happiness upon him,
For then, and not till then, he felt himself,
And found the blessedness of being little.
