And all the clouds that loured upon our house
In the deep bosom of the ocean buried.
quotes.plain: Sometimes the hard season ends. The dark clouds can go to the bottom of the sea.

quotes.text:
They that stand high have many blasts to shake them,
And if they fall they dash themselves to pieces.
quotes.plain: The higher you stand the more wind hits you, and a fall from there breaks you.

quotes.text:
Sorrow breaks seasons and reposing hours,
Makes the night morning, and the noontide night.
quotes.plain: Sorrow takes over the clock. The night feels like morning and noon feels like night.

quotes.text:
Why grow the branches when the root is gone?
Why wither not the leaves that want their sap?
quotes.plain: Grief makes no sense of the world going on after you lose what fed you.

quotes.text:
Sister, have comfort. All of us have cause
To wail the dimming of our shining star,
But none can help our harms by wailing them.
quotes.plain: Crying about the damage doesn't fix it.
Read the signs early. Smart people prepare before the storm hits.

quotes.text:
And since, methinks I would not grow so fast,
Because sweet flowers are slow and weeds make haste.
quotes.plain: Fast growth isn't a sign of quality. The good stuff takes its time.

quotes.text:
Sweet prince, the untainted virtue of your years
Hath not yet dived into the world’s deceit,
Nor more can you distinguish of a man
Than of his outward show, which, God He knows,
Seldom or never jumpeth with the heart.
quotes.plain: People's faces and their hearts rarely match. Judge them by what they do.

quotes.text: So wise so young, they say, do never live long.
quotes.plain: The kid who sees too much too early burns out. Watch the pace.

quotes.text:
Death makes no conquest of this conqueror,
For now he lives in fame, though not in life.
quotes.plain: Do something worth remembering and death only gets half of you.

quotes.text: Short summers lightly have a forward spring.
quotes.plain: A rushed start often means a short run.

quotes.text:
’Tis a vile thing to die, my gracious lord,
When men are unprepared and look not for it.
quotes.plain: The worst way to be caught is feeling safe.

quotes.text:
O momentary grace of mortal men,
Which we more hunt for than the grace of God!
Who builds his hope in air of your good looks
Lives like a drunken sailor on a mast,
Ready with every nod to tumble down
Into the fatal bowels of the deep.
quotes.plain: Live off other people's approval and you're one frown from the floor.

quotes.text:
Here’s a good world the while! Who is so gross
That cannot see this palpable device?
Yet who so bold but says he sees it not?
quotes.plain: Everyone sees the con and nobody says it out loud.

quotes.text:
Eighty odd years of sorrow have I seen,
And each hour’s joy wracked with a week of teen.
quotes.plain: A long life where every hour of joy cost a week of grief.
Overthinking becomes delay and delay becomes poverty. Move.

quotes.text:
So now prosperity begins to mellow,
And drop into the rotten mouth of death.
quotes.plain: Success ripens fast and rots just as fast.

quotes.text:
Thus hath the course of justice wheeled about
And left thee but a very prey to time,
Having no more but thought of what thou wast
To torture thee the more, being what thou art.
quotes.plain: Remembering who you were is the cruelest part of falling.

quotes.text:
Let them have scope, though what they do impart
Help nothing else, yet do they ease the heart.
quotes.plain: Words fix nothing, but saying them out loud still lightens the load.

quotes.text:
Look what is done cannot be now amended.
Men shall deal unadvisedly sometimes,
Which after-hours gives leisure to repent.
quotes.plain: You can't undo it. Regret comes later, after the damage.

quotes.text: An honest tale speeds best being plainly told.
quotes.plain: The truth goes further when you say it straight.

quotes.text:
That high All-Seer which I dallied with
Hath turned my feigned prayer on my head
And given in earnest what I begged in jest.
quotes.plain: Careful what you toy with. It can take you at your word.

quotes.text:
True hope is swift, and flies with swallow’s wings;
Kings it makes gods, and meaner creatures kings.
quotes.plain: Real hope moves fast and lifts everyone who carries it.

quotes.text:
Let’s lack no discipline, make no delay,
For, lords, tomorrow is a busy day.
quotes.plain: Be ready tonight, because tomorrow won't wait.

quotes.text:
What do I fear? Myself? There’s none else by.
Richard loves Richard, that is, I am I.
quotes.plain: Alone at night, the only thing you're afraid of is yourself.

quotes.text:
My conscience hath a thousand several tongues,
And every tongue brings in a several tale,
And every tale condemns me for a villain.
quotes.plain: Your conscience talks louder at night than any enemy.

quotes.text:
By the apostle Paul, shadows tonight
Have struck more terror to the soul of Richard
Than can the substance of ten thousand soldiers
Armed in proof and led by shallow Richmond.
quotes.plain: Fear of imagined things can hit harder than a real army.

quotes.text:
Conscience is but a word that cowards use,
Devised at first to keep the strong in awe.
Our strong arms be our conscience, swords our law.
quotes.plain: The tyrant's excuse for everything. It also doesn't save him.

quotes.text: A horse! A horse! My kingdom for a horse!
quotes.plain: At the critical moment, everything you built is worth less than one small thing you lack.

quotes.text:
Slave, I have set my life upon a cast,
And I will stand the hazard of the die.
quotes.plain: All in on one throw, and I'll live with the roll.

quotes.text:
Two households, both alike in dignity,
In fair Verona, where we lay our scene,
From ancient grudge break to new mutiny,
Where civil blood makes civil hands unclean.
quotes.plain: Old grudges outlive the people who started them and keep spilling blood.

quotes.text:
Why, then, O brawling love! O loving hate!
O anything, of nothing first create!
O heavy lightness! serious vanity!
Misshapen chaos of well-seeming forms!
Feather of lead, bright smoke, cold fire, sick health!
Still-waking sleep, that is not what it is!
quotes.plain: Love feels like opposites at once. It's chaos dressed up nice.
Love is a sweet madness that also chokes you.
A new fire puts out the old one. Turn around and look somewhere else.

quotes.text:
Not I, believe me, you have dancing shoes,
With nimble soles, I have a soul of lead
So stakes me to the ground I cannot move.
quotes.plain: Some days the heart is lead and you can't move.

quotes.text:
I mean sir, in delay
We waste our lights in vain, light lights by day.
quotes.plain: Waiting around burns your light for nothing.

quotes.text:
True, I talk of dreams,
Which are the children of an idle brain,
Begot of nothing but vain fantasy,
Which is as thin of substance as the air,
And more inconstant than the wind, who woos
Even now the frozen bosom of the north,
And, being anger’d, puffs away from thence,
Turning his side to the dew-dropping south.
quotes.plain: Dreams are made of nothing and shift like the wind. Don't live in them.

quotes.text:
Did my heart love till now? Forswear it, sight!
For I ne’er saw true beauty till this night.
quotes.plain: Everything before this was practice.

quotes.text:
My only love sprung from my only hate!
Too early seen unknown, and known too late!
quotes.plain: You can fall for the one person you were never supposed to.

quotes.text: He jests at scars that never felt a wound.
quotes.plain: People who've never been hurt mock those who have.

quotes.text:
What’s in a name? That which we call a rose
By any other name would smell as sweet;
So Romeo would, were he not Romeo call’d,
Retain that dear perfection which he owes
Without that title.
quotes.plain: A label doesn't change what a thing is. You are not your family name.

quotes.text:
My bounty is as boundless as the sea,
My love as deep; the more I give to thee,
The more I have, for both are infinite.
quotes.plain: Giving love doesn't use it up. The more you give, the more you have.

quotes.text:
Love goes toward love as schoolboys from their books,
But love from love, towards school with heavy looks.
quotes.plain: You run toward what you want and drag your feet away from it.

quotes.text:
Good night, good night. Parting is such sweet sorrow
That I shall say good night till it be morrow.
quotes.plain: Leaving hurts because what you're leaving was good.

quotes.text:
Virtue itself turns vice being misapplied,
And vice sometime’s by action dignified.
quotes.plain: Even good things go bad in the wrong use, and bad things can serve a purpose.

quotes.text:
Care keeps his watch in every old man’s eye,
And where care lodges sleep will never lie;
But where unbruised youth with unstuff’d brain
Doth couch his limbs, there golden sleep doth reign.
quotes.plain: Worry steals sleep. A clear mind sleeps like a kid.

quotes.text: Wisely and slow; they stumble that run fast.
quotes.plain: Rushing is how you trip. Go steady.

quotes.text:
The excuse that thou dost make in this delay
Is longer than the tale thou dost excuse.
quotes.plain: Your excuse for putting it off takes longer than the thing itself.

quotes.text:
These violent delights have violent ends,
And in their triumph die; like fire and powder,
Which as they kiss consume. The sweetest honey
Is loathsome in his own deliciousness,
And in the taste confounds the appetite.
Therefore love moderately: long love doth so;
Too swift arrives as tardy as too slow.
quotes.plain: Intense highs burn out. Pace yourself and the good thing lasts.
When something is real you can't put a number on it.

quotes.text: No, ’tis not so deep as a well, nor so wide as a church door, but ’tis enough, ’twill serve. Ask for me tomorrow, and you shall find me a grave man.
quotes.plain: Even dying, he jokes. Wit is the last thing to go.

quotes.text:
This day’s black fate on mo days doth depend;
This but begins the woe others must end.
quotes.plain: One bad day sets off a chain of more. Be careful what you start.

quotes.text: O, I am fortune’s fool!
quotes.plain: One bad day and you feel like the plaything of fate.

quotes.text:
Come gentle night, come loving black-brow’d night,
Give me my Romeo, and when I shall die,
Take him and cut him out in little stars,
And he will make the face of heaven so fine
That all the world will be in love with night,
And pay no worship to the garish sun.
quotes.plain: Love so strong it would turn a person into the stars.

quotes.text:
Was ever book containing such vile matter
So fairly bound? O, that deceit should dwell
In such a gorgeous palace.
quotes.plain: A beautiful cover can hide something ugly. Looks prove nothing.

quotes.text:
Affliction is enanmour’d of thy parts
And thou art wedded to calamity.
quotes.plain: When you're deep in hardship, it feels like it picked you on purpose.

quotes.text: Be patient, for the world is broad and wide.
quotes.plain: Your bad spot is not the whole map. There is somewhere else to go.

quotes.text: Thou canst not speak of that thou dost not feel.
quotes.plain: Advice from someone who hasn't been there doesn't land.

quotes.text:
Fie, fie, thou sham’st thy shape, thy love, thy wit,
Which, like a usurer, abound’st in all,
And usest none in that true use indeed
Which should bedeck thy shape, thy love, thy wit.
quotes.plain: You have gifts and you're wasting them while you wallow. Use them.

quotes.text:
Night’s candles are burnt out, and jocund day
Stands tiptoe on the misty mountain tops.
I must be gone and live, or stay and die.
quotes.plain: Morning means leave. Staying comfortable has a cost.

quotes.text:
O Fortune, Fortune! All men call thee fickle,
If thou art fickle, what dost thou with him
That is renown’d for faith? Be fickle, Fortune;
For then, I hope thou wilt not keep him long
But send him back.
quotes.plain: If luck is fickle, let it be fickle in my favor.

quotes.text: What must be shall be.
quotes.plain: Some things are coming whether you fight them or not.

quotes.text: Love give me strength, and strength shall help afford.
quotes.plain: Ask for strength and then act on it.

quotes.text:
I have a faint cold fear thrills through my veins
That almost freezes up the heat of life.
quotes.plain: The moment right before a big step, fear goes cold.

quotes.text:
Death lies on her like an untimely frost
Upon the sweetest flower of all the field.
quotes.plain: Death takes the young and good out of season.

quotes.text:
All things that we ordained festival
Turn from their office to black funeral:
Our instruments to melancholy bells,
Our wedding cheer to a sad burial feast;
Our solemn hymns to sullen dirges change;
Our bridal flowers serve for a buried corse,
And all things change them to the contrary.
quotes.plain: Everything planned for joy can flip overnight. Nothing is guaranteed.

quotes.text:
Ah me, how sweet is love itself possess’d,
When but love’s shadows are so rich in joy.
quotes.plain: If the dream of it feels this good, the real thing is something else.

quotes.text: Is it even so? Then I defy you, stars!
quotes.plain: Fate hits, and you throw your fist up at the sky.

quotes.text:
There is thy gold, worse poison to men’s souls,
Doing more murder in this loathsome world
Than these poor compounds that thou mayst not sell.
quotes.plain: Money kills more people than any drug does.

quotes.text:
See what a scourge is laid upon your hate,
That heaven finds means to kill your joys with love!
quotes.plain: Feuds end up costing you what you loved most.

quotes.text:
Go hence, to have more talk of these sad things.
Some shall be pardon’d, and some punished,
For never was a story of more woe
Than this of Juliet and her Romeo.
quotes.plain: The famous last word on a story of love undone by hate.

quotes.text: Come, madam wife, sit by my side and let the world slip: we shall ne’er be younger.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 0 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Let the small stuff go. You're never younger than right now.

quotes.text:
Only, good master, while we do admire
This virtue and this moral discipline,
Let’s be no stoics nor no stocks, I pray;
Or so devote to Aristotle’s checks
As Ovid be an outcast quite abjur’d.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Discipline is good but don't turn into a statue. Leave room for life.

quotes.text:
No profit grows where is no pleasure ta’en;
In brief, sir, study what you most affect.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: You get nothing out of work you hate. Chase what pulls you.

quotes.text:
Think you a little din can daunt mine ears?
Have I not in my time heard lions roar?
Have I not heard the sea, puff’d up with winds,
Rage like an angry boar chafed with sweat?
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 1 Scene 2
quotes.plain: After real storms, small noise doesn't scare you.

quotes.text:
Ay, to the proof, as mountains are for winds,
That shake not though they blow perpetually.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 2 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Be the mountain. Let the wind blow forever.

quotes.text:
I see a woman may be made a fool,
If she had not a spirit to resist.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 3 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Anyone gets pushed around if they don't have the spirit to push back.

quotes.text:
Your betters have endur’d me say my mind,
And if you cannot, best you stop your ears.
My tongue will tell the anger of my heart,
Or else my heart, concealing it, will break;
And rather than it shall, I will be free
Even to the uttermost, as I please, in words.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 4 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Swallowing your anger eats you. Say what's true.

quotes.text:
Our purses shall be proud, our garments poor
For ’tis the mind that makes the body rich;
And as the sun breaks through the darkest clouds,
So honour peereth in the meanest habit.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 4 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Wealth is in the mind. Worth shows through even plain clothes.

quotes.text:
What, is the jay more precious than the lark
Because his feathers are more beautiful?
Or is the adder better than the eel
Because his painted skin contents the eye?
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 4 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Flashy doesn't mean better.

quotes.text: Dally not with the gods, but get thee gone.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 4 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Stop praying about it and go act.

quotes.text:
But now I see our lances are but straws,
Our strength as weak, our weakness past compare,
That seeming to be most which we indeed least are.
quotes.location: The Taming of the Shrew, Act 5 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Your show of strength can hide how weak you really are. Know the difference.

quotes.text: What cares these roarers for the name of king?
quotes.plain: A storm doesn't care what title you hold. Only the work in front of you counts.

quotes.text:
What seest thou else
In the dark backward and abysm of time?
quotes.plain: Look back far enough and the past turns dark and dreamlike. So don't live there.

quotes.text:
I find my zenith doth depend upon
A most auspicious star, whose influence
If now I court not but omit, my fortunes
Will ever after droop.
quotes.plain: Your big chance has a window. Court it now or it's gone for good.

quotes.text:
All but mariners
Plunged in the foaming brine and quit the vessel,
Then all afire with me: the King’s son, Ferdinand,
With hair up-staring, then like reeds, not hair, Was the first man that leapt; cried “Hell is empty,
And all the devils are here.”
quotes.plain: When the fear peaks, it feels like everything bad has shown up at once. It passes.

quotes.text:
Nothing of him that doth fade
But doth suffer a sea-change
Into something rich and strange.
quotes.plain: Even loss changes you into something new and valuable.

quotes.text:
They are both in either’s powers. But this swift business
I must uneasy make, lest too light winning
Make the prize light.
quotes.plain: What comes too easy gets treated cheap. Some difficulty is what gives a thing its worth.

quotes.text:
The truth you speak doth lack some gentleness
And time to speak it in. You rub the sore,
When you should bring the plaster.
quotes.plain: Being right is not enough. Timing and kindness decide whether the truth helps or just hurts.

quotes.text:
Do not omit the heavy offer of it:
It seldom visits sorrow; when it doth,
It is a comforter.
quotes.plain: Sleep rarely comes to the grieving. When it does, take it.

quotes.text:
Ebbing men indeed,
Most often, do so near the bottom run
By their own fear or sloth.
quotes.plain: Most people who sink low got there through fear or laziness, not bad luck.

quotes.text:
And by that destiny, to perform an act
Whereof what’s past is prologue, what to come
In yours and my discharge.
quotes.plain: Everything behind you is only the setup. What happens next is up to you.

quotes.text: My best way is to creep under his gaberdine; there is no other shelter hereabout: misery acquaints a man with strange bed-fellows.
quotes.plain: When you're desperate you'll take shelter wherever you find it, even with people you'd never choose.

quotes.text:
There be some sports are painful, and their labour
Delight in them sets off: some kinds of baseness
Are nobly undergone; and most poor matters
Point to rich ends.
quotes.plain: Hard, low work is worth it when it leads somewhere good, and wanting the goal makes it lighter.

quotes.text:
The isle is full of noises,
Sounds, and sweet airs, that give delight, and hurt not.
quotes.plain: What you fear in the dark is often just sound. Much of it is meant to be beautiful.

quotes.text:
Sometimes a thousand twangling instruments
Will hum about mine ears; and sometimes voices,
That, if I then had wak’d after long sleep,
Will make me sleep again: and then, in dreaming,
The clouds methought would open and show riches
Ready to drop upon me; that, when I wak’d,
I cried to dream again.
quotes.plain: Some dreams are so good that waking up hurts. Let them point you at what you want.

quotes.text:
All three of them are desperate: their great guilt,
Like poison given to work a great time after,
Now ’gins to bite the spirits.
quotes.plain: Guilt works slowly, like a delayed poison, and it always comes due.

quotes.text:
Look thou be true; do not give dalliance
Too much the rein: the strongest oaths are straw
To th’ fire i’ the blood: be more abstemious,
Or else good night your vow!
quotes.plain: Promises are weak against desire. Stay stricter than you think you need to.

quotes.text:
And, like the baseless fabric of this vision,
The cloud-capp’d towers, the gorgeous palaces,
The solemn temples, the great globe itself,
Yea, all which it inherit, shall dissolve,
And, like this insubstantial pageant faded,
Leave not a rack behind.
quotes.plain: Towers, palaces and temples all dissolve. Nothing you build is permanent, so build with that in mind.

quotes.text:
We are such stuff
As dreams are made on, and our little life
Is rounded with a sleep.
quotes.plain: Life is brief and dreamlike, ending in sleep. Spend it on purpose.

quotes.text:
Though with their high wrongs I am struck to th’ quick,
Yet with my nobler reason ’gainst my fury
Do I take part: the rarer action is
In virtue than in vengeance: they being penitent,
The sole drift of my purpose doth extend
Not a frown further.
quotes.plain: Getting even is easy. Letting it go takes real strength.

quotes.text:
Though the seas threaten, they are merciful.
I have curs’d them without cause.
quotes.plain: What looked like the thing trying to destroy you may have carried you to shore.

quotes.text:
How beauteous mankind is! O brave new world
That has such people in ’t!
quotes.plain: Seeing the world fresh, before you've been burned by it, is a gift worth protecting.

quotes.text:
Let us not burden our remembrances with
A heaviness that’s gone.
quotes.plain: Don't drag old pain into the present. It's over, so put it down.

quotes.text:
O, rejoice
Beyond a common joy, and set it down
With gold on lasting pillars: in one voyage
Did Claribel her husband find at Tunis,
And Ferdinand, her brother, found a wife
Where he himself was lost; Prospero his dukedom
In a poor isle; and all of us ourselves,
When no man was his own.
quotes.plain: Sometimes it takes losing everything to find yourself.

quotes.text:
Two of these fellows you
Must know and own; this thing of darkness I
Acknowledge mine.
quotes.plain: Own your dark side. Pretending it belongs to someone else keeps it in charge.

quotes.text:
What a thrice-double ass
Was I, to take this drunkard for a god,
And worship this dull fool!
quotes.plain: Admitting you worshipped the wrong thing is the first step to wising up.

quotes.text:
And thence retire me to my Milan, where
Every third thought shall be my grave.
quotes.plain: Keep death in your thoughts often. It sharpens what you do with the day.

quotes.text:
When Fortune in her shift and change of mood
Spurns down her late beloved, all his dependants,
Which laboured after him to the mountain’s top
Even on their knees and hands, let him slip down,
Not one accompanying his declining foot.
quotes.plain: When your luck turns, the people who climbed up with you are the first to leave.

quotes.text:
’Tis not enough to help the feeble up,
But to support him after.
quotes.plain: Pulling someone up is half the job. Staying with them is the other half.

quotes.text: He that loves to be flattered is worthy o’ th’ flatterer.
quotes.plain: If you crave flattery, you deserve the liars it attracts.

quotes.text: Time to be honest.
quotes.plain: Whatever you've been dodging, now is the time to say it.

quotes.text:
I should fear those that dance before me now
Would one day stamp upon me. ’T has been done.
Men shut their doors against a setting sun.
quotes.plain: People celebrate you while you're rising and close the door when you fall. Know who is who.

quotes.text:
O, that men’s ears should be
To counsel deaf, but not to flattery!
quotes.plain: People ignore hard advice and swallow flattery. Don't be one of them.
Even the whole world could be spent in a breath. Money is easy to lose.

quotes.text:
Ah, when the means are gone that buy this praise,
The breath is gone whereof this praise is made.
Feast-won, fast-lost; one cloud of winter showers,
These flies are couched.
quotes.plain: Praise bought with money disappears when the money does. Easy come, easy go.

quotes.text:
You must consider that a prodigal course
Is like the sun’s, but not like his recoverable.
quotes.plain: The sun sets and rises again. Spent money doesn't.

quotes.text: Nothing emboldens sin so much as mercy.
quotes.plain: When bad behavior has no cost, it grows. Hold lines, including with yourself.

quotes.text:
He’s truly valiant that can wisely suffer
The worst that man can breathe, and make his wrongs
His outsides to wear them like his raiment, carelessly,
And ne’er prefer his injuries to his heart,
To bring it into danger.
quotes.plain: The strong person takes the hit and keeps it from reaching the heart, instead of fighting every insult.

quotes.text:
To be in anger is impiety,
But who is man that is not angry?
quotes.plain: Anger is wrong, but nobody is free of it. Own it and manage it.

quotes.text:
With his disease of all-shunned poverty,
Walks, like contempt, alone.
quotes.plain: Being broke can isolate you more than anything, because people stop calling.

quotes.text: Keep it, I cannot eat it.
quotes.plain: Gold doesn't fill you up. Know what money can't buy.

quotes.text:
Willing misery
Outlives incertain pomp, is crowned before;
The one is filling still, never complete,
The other, at high wish. Best state, contentless,
Hath a distracted and most wretched being,
Worse than the worst, content.
quotes.plain: Wanting more never fills you up. Someone with little who is at peace beats someone with everything who is never satisfied.

quotes.text: The middle of humanity thou never knewest, but the extremity of both ends.
quotes.plain: You only know the top and the bottom. Learn the steady middle.

quotes.text: There is no time so miserable but a man may be true.
quotes.plain: Hard times never excuse being fake. You can always stay honest.

quotes.text:
What viler thing upon the earth than friends
Who can bring noblest minds to basest ends!
quotes.plain: False friends can drag a good person down faster than any enemy.

quotes.text:
You should have feared false times when you did feast,
Suspect still comes where an estate is least.
quotes.plain: Doubt and suspicion show up when you're broke, which is when it's too late. Watch people while times are good.

quotes.text: Promising is the very air o’ th’ time; it opens the eyes of expectation.
quotes.plain: People hand out promises like air. Do the thing instead and you stand out.

quotes.text:
Then do we sin against our own estate
When we may profit meet and come too late.
quotes.plain: Let a good opening pass and you wrong yourself. Move while it's open.

quotes.text: Let it go naked. Men may see’t the better.
quotes.plain: Plain truth, undressed, is easiest to see.

quotes.text:
At all times alike
Men are not still the same: ’twas time and griefs
That framed him thus.
quotes.plain: People are not fixed. Time and pain shape them, and time can heal what it bent.

quotes.text:
Crimes, like lands,
Are not inherited.
quotes.plain: You don't owe for what someone before you did. Neither does anyone else.

quotes.text:
Wilt thou draw near the nature of the gods?
Draw near them then in being merciful.
Sweet mercy is nobility’s true badge.
quotes.plain: Mercy is what makes a strong person noble.

quotes.text:
Give me a staff of honour for mine age,
But not a sceptre to control the world.
quotes.plain: Pick respect over rule. A walking staff beats a scepter.

quotes.text:
Sorrow concealed, like an oven stopped,
Doth burn the heart to cinders where it is.
quotes.plain: Pain you keep sealed up burns you from the inside. Talk, write, let it out.

quotes.text:
Why, foolish Lucius, dost thou not perceive
That Rome is but a wilderness of tigers?
quotes.plain: Sometimes being thrown out of a bad place is a lucky break.

quotes.text:
If there were reason for these miseries,
Then into limits could I bind my woes.
quotes.plain: Grief has no logic, so don't expect yourself to reason your way out of it.

quotes.text:
Then give me leave, for losers will have leave
To ease their stomachs with their bitter tongues.
quotes.plain: People who lost something need to say it out loud. Let them, and let yourself.

quotes.text:
To weep with them that weep doth ease some deal,
But sorrow flouted at is double death.
quotes.plain: Shared sorrow helps. Being laughed at in your sorrow is twice as bad.

quotes.text:
Why, I have not another tear to shed.
Besides, this sorrow is an enemy,
And would usurp upon my watery eyes,
And make them blind with tributary tears.
quotes.plain: Grief can blind you. At some point you have to stop crying and decide what to do.
We're not giants, we're tough, and we're carrying more than anyone should.

quotes.text:
Why should I war without the walls of Troy
That find such cruel battle here within?
Each Trojan that is master of his heart,
Let him to field; Troilus, alas! hath none.
quotes.plain: There's no use winning outside while you're losing the fight inside. Master yourself first.

quotes.text: He that will have a cake out of the wheat must tarry the grinding.
quotes.plain: Anything worth having has steps you can't skip. Wait through the grinding.

quotes.text:
I was about to tell thee: when my heart,
As wedged with a sigh, would rive in twain,
Lest Hector or my father should perceive me,
I have, as when the sun doth light a storm,
Buried this sigh in wrinkle of a smile.
But sorrow that is couch’d in seeming gladness
Is like that mirth fate turns to sudden sadness.
quotes.plain: You can smile over a heavy chest, but hidden sorrow only turns sharper.

quotes.text: Well, the gods are above; time must friend or end.
quotes.plain: Time will settle it one way or the other. Do what you can and let it work.

quotes.text:
Things won are done; joy’s soul lies in the doing.
That she belov’d knows naught that knows not this:
Men prize the thing ungain’d more than it is.
quotes.plain: The chase is sweeter than the catch. We overvalue what we haven't got yet.

quotes.text:
In the reproof of chance
Lies the true proof of men.
quotes.plain: Adversity is the test. Calm seas prove nothing about a person.

quotes.text:
Take but degree away, untune that string,
And hark what discord follows!
quotes.plain: Remove order and discipline and everything falls into noise.

quotes.text:
And appetite, an universal wolf,
So doubly seconded with will and power,
Must make perforce an universal prey,
And last eat up himself.
quotes.plain: Unchecked appetite with power behind it ends up devouring itself.

quotes.text: What’s aught but as ’tis valued?
quotes.plain: Things are worth what you decide they are worth.

quotes.text:
O theft most base,
That we have stol’n what we do fear to keep!
quotes.plain: The worst kind of shame is grabbing something and then being scared to hold it.

quotes.text:
Thus to persist
In doing wrong extenuates not wrong,
But makes it much more heavy.
quotes.plain: Doubling down on a wrong does not shrink it. It makes it heavier.

quotes.text: The amity that wisdom knits not, folly may easily untie.
quotes.plain: What wisdom ties together, one foolish move can undo.

quotes.text:
A stirring dwarf we do allowance give
Before a sleeping giant.
quotes.plain: A small man in motion is worth more than a giant lying down.

quotes.text: He that is proud eats up himself. Pride is his own glass, his own trumpet, his own chronicle; and whatever praises itself but in the deed devours the deed in the praise.
quotes.plain: Pride feeds on itself. Praising your own work eats the work.

quotes.text: Blind fear, that seeing reason leads, finds safer footing than blind reason stumbling without fear. To fear the worst oft cures the worse.
quotes.plain: Fear that sees clearly beats confidence that sees nothing. Expecting the worst often heads it off.

quotes.text: This is the monstruosity in love, lady, that the will is infinite, and the execution confin’d; that the desire is boundless, and the act a slave to limit.
quotes.plain: Wanting has no ceiling. What you can actually do always does.

quotes.text:
’Tis certain, greatness, once fall’n out with fortune,
Must fall out with men too.
quotes.plain: When your luck turns, people turn with it.

quotes.text:
Time hath, my lord, a wallet at his back,
Wherein he puts alms for oblivion,
A great-siz’d monster of ingratitudes.
Those scraps are good deeds past, which are devour’d
As fast as they are made, forgot as soon
As done. Perseverance, dear my lord,
Keeps honour bright.
quotes.plain: Time forgets what you did yesterday. Only showing up again keeps your name alive.

quotes.text:
The welcome ever smiles,
And farewell goes out sighing. O, let not virtue seek
Remuneration for the thing it was;
For beauty, wit,
High birth, vigour of bone, desert in service,
Love, friendship, charity, are subjects all
To envious and calumniating Time.
quotes.plain: Everyone greets the new thing and forgets the old. Beauty, wit and even friendship are at time's mercy.

quotes.text:
One touch of nature makes the whole world kin, That all with one consent praise new-born gauds,
Though they are made and moulded of things past,
And give to dust that is a little gilt
More laud than gilt o’er-dusted.
quotes.plain: People rush to praise what is shiny and new, even if it is made of old stuff.
The damage you do yourself by sitting out heals worst. Doing nothing is a choice with a price.

quotes.text:
My mind is troubled, like a fountain stirr’d;
And I myself see not the bottom of it.
quotes.plain: When your mind is churning you cannot see to the bottom of it.

quotes.text:
And sometimes we are devils to ourselves,
When we will tempt the frailty of our powers,
Presuming on their changeful potency.
quotes.plain: We can be our own devil by testing how strong we really are.

quotes.text:
What’s past and what’s to come is strew’d with husks
And formless ruin of oblivion;
quotes.plain: The past and the future are rubble. Only this moment is solid.
Judge it at the end. Time settles every argument eventually.

quotes.text:
Mine honour keeps the weather of my fate.
Life every man holds dear; but the dear man
Holds honour far more precious dear than life.
quotes.plain: Everyone holds life dear, but a man of honour holds his word dearer.

quotes.text:
Words, words, mere words, no matter from the heart;
Th’effect doth operate another way.
quotes.plain: Words are cheap. What matters is what the heart actually does.

quotes.text:
Dexterity so obeying appetite
That what he will he does, and does so much
That proof is call’d impossibility.
quotes.plain: When skill and will line up, the thing you do gets called impossible.

quotes.text:
I do not speak of flight, of fear of death,
But dare all imminence that gods and men
Address their dangers in.
quotes.plain: Don't let fear of death make your choices.

quotes.text:
If music be the food of love, play on,
Give me excess of it; that, surfeiting,
The appetite may sicken and so die.
quotes.plain: Overdo what you crave and the craving dies on its own.

quotes.text:
So full of shapes is fancy,
That it alone is high fantastical.
quotes.plain: Desire changes shape constantly. Nothing it takes in keeps its value for long.

quotes.text:
What else may hap, to time I will commit;
Only shape thou thy silence to my wit.
quotes.plain: What happens, happens. Leave it to time and keep your mouth shut.

quotes.text: Better a witty fool than a foolish wit.
quotes.plain: Better to be a clever fool than a stupid wise man.

quotes.text:
Fate, show thy force, ourselves we do not owe.
What is decreed must be; and be this so!
quotes.plain: You don't control how it plays out. Face it anyway.

quotes.text:
But come what may, I do adore thee so,
That danger shall seem sport, and I will go.
quotes.plain: Come what may, I love you enough that danger looks like play.

quotes.text:
Alas, our frailty is the cause, not we,
For such as we are made of, such we be.
quotes.plain: We are made the way we are made. The fault is in the material, not the person.

quotes.text:
O time, thou must untangle this, not I,
It is too hard a knot for me t’untie!
quotes.plain: Some knots are too tight for you to untie. Let time do it.

quotes.text:
What is love? ’Tis not hereafter,
Present mirth hath present laughter.
What’s to come is still unsure.
In delay there lies no plenty,
Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty.
Youth’s a stuff will not endure.
quotes.plain: Enjoy now. The future is uncertain and youth does not last.

quotes.text: Dost thou think, because thou art virtuous, there shall be no more cakes and ale?
quotes.plain: Just because you live clean does not mean everyone else has to quit the fun.

quotes.text:
She never told her love,
But let concealment, like a worm i’ th’ bud,
Feed on her damask cheek: she pined in thought,
And with a green and yellow melancholy
She sat like patience on a monument,
Smiling at grief.
quotes.plain: She never said it and it ate her alive. Silence about what you feel does damage.

quotes.text: In my stars I am above thee, but be not afraid of greatness. Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon ’em.
quotes.plain: Some are born great, some earn it, some get it dropped on them. Do not be afraid of greatness.

quotes.text: Foolery, sir, does walk about the orb like the sun; it shines everywhere.
quotes.plain: Foolishness is everywhere, like the sun. Nobody is above it.

quotes.text:
A murd’rous guilt shows not itself more soon
Than love that would seem hid. Love’s night is noon.
quotes.plain: Guilt shows itself fast, and so does love you are trying to hide.

quotes.text: Love sought is good, but given unsought is better.
quotes.plain: Love you chase is good. Love that comes to you unasked is better.

quotes.text:
In nature there’s no blemish but the mind;
None can be call’d deform’d but the unkind.
Virtue is beauty, but the beauteous evil
Are empty trunks, o’erflourished by the devil.
quotes.plain: The only real ugliness is a cold heart. Good looks can hide a rotten person.

quotes.text: I say there is no darkness but ignorance, in which thou art more puzzled than the Egyptians in their fog.
quotes.plain: The only real darkness is not knowing.

quotes.text: Now my foes tell me plainly I am an ass: so that by my foes, sir, I profit in the knowledge of myself, and by my friends I am abused.
quotes.plain: Enemies tell you the truth about yourself. Friends flatter you into being a fool.

quotes.text:
Alas, it is the baseness of thy fear
That makes thee strangle thy propriety.
Fear not, Cesario, take thy fortunes up.
Be that thou know’st thou art, and then thou art
As great as that thou fear’st.
quotes.plain: Fear is what keeps you small. Be who you know you are and you are as big as the thing you fear.

quotes.text: And thus the whirligig of time brings in his revenges.
quotes.plain: Time turns and everyone gets paid back eventually.

quotes.text: Home-keeping youth have ever homely wits.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Staying put makes you dull. You get sharp by going out.

quotes.text:
To be in love, where scorn is bought with groans,
Coy looks with heart-sore sighs, one fading moment’s mirth
With twenty watchful, weary, tedious nights.
If haply won, perhaps a hapless gain;
If lost, why then a grievous labour won;
However, but a folly bought with wit,
Or else a wit by folly vanquished.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Chasing love often costs more than it pays: it is a folly bought with wit, or wit beaten by folly.

quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: If love is your master and you obey it, do not expect to be called wise.

quotes.text:
Thou, Julia, thou hast metamorphosed me,
Made me neglect my studies, lose my time,
War with good counsel, set the world at nought;
Made wit with musing weak, heart sick with thought.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Infatuation made me neglect my work, waste my time, and ignore good advice. My mind went weak.

quotes.text:
I have no other but a woman’s reason:
I think him so because I think him so.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Sometimes the only reason is a feeling, and you cannot argue it.

quotes.text: Fire that’s closest kept burns most of all.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 2
quotes.plain: The fire you keep hidden burns hottest.

quotes.text:
Fie, fie, how wayward is this foolish love
That like a testy babe will scratch the nurse
And presently, all humbled, kiss the rod!
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Love makes you lash out at what you want, then crawl back and take the punishment.

quotes.text:
Experience is by industry achieved
And perfected by the swift course of time.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Experience comes from hard work and then time finishes it.

quotes.text:
Thus have I shunned the fire for fear of burning
And drenched me in the sea, where I am drowned.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Dodging the fire, I walked into the sea and drowned.

quotes.text:
O, how this spring of love resembleth
The uncertain glory of an April day,
Which now shows all the beauty of the sun,
And by an by a cloud takes all away.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 1 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Good things can be gone in a moment, like a cloud taking the sun on an April day.

quotes.text:
Except I be by Silvia in the night,
There is no music in the nightingale.
Unless I look on Silvia in the day,
There is no day for me to look upon.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 3 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Without the person you love, the whole world goes silent and dark.

quotes.text:
Cease to lament for that thou canst not help,
And study help for that which thou lament’st.
Time is the nurse and breeder of all good.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 3 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Stop mourning what you cannot help and work on what you can. Time heals most things.

quotes.text:
Hope is a lover’s staff; walk hence with that
And manage it against despairing thoughts.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 3 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Hope is the staff you walk with. Use it against despair.

quotes.text: But love will not be spurred to what it loathes.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Love cannot be forced.

quotes.text:
A thousand more mischances than this one
Have learned me how to brook this patiently.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 3
quotes.plain: A thousand worse breaks than this one taught me how to take it calmly.

quotes.text: How use doth breed a habit in a man!
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Habit builds itself in you without asking.

quotes.text:
The private wound is deepest. O time most accurst,
’Mongst all foes that a friend should be the worst!
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: The deepest cuts come from a friend.

quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Real remorse deserves forgiveness. Refusing it puts you out of step with heaven and earth.

quotes.text:
O heaven, were man
But constant, he were perfect. That one error
Fills him with faults, makes him run through all th’ sins;
Inconstancy falls off ere it begins.
quotes.location: The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: A person who stayed constant would be perfect. Wavering is the one flaw that breeds all the others.

quotes.text:
O grief and time,
Fearful consumers, you will all devour!
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Grief and time eat everything in the end.

quotes.text:
Extremity, that sharpens sundry wits,
Makes me a fool.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Extreme pain sharpens some minds and turns others into fools. Do not judge people in it.

quotes.text:
Who cannot feel nor see the rain, being in ’t,
Knows neither wet nor dry.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: If you are standing in it, you cannot feel the rain. You are too deep to see it.

quotes.text:
As we are men,
Thus should we do; being sensually subdued,
We lose our human title.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 1
quotes.plain: We are men only while we stay in control of ourselves. Lose control and you lose that.

quotes.text:
Let th’ event,
That never-erring arbitrator, tell us
When we know all ourselves; and let us follow
The becking of our chance.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Outcomes are the only honest judge. Do the work, then let results tell you who you are.

quotes.text:
Their knot of love,
Tied, weaved, entangled, with so true, so long,
And with a finger of so deep a cunning,
May be outworn, never undone.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 3
quotes.plain: A bond built over years can wear thin, but it does not come apart.

quotes.text:
This world’s a city full of straying streets,
And death’s the market-place where each one meets.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 1 Scene 5
quotes.plain: Everyone takes a different road, and every road ends in the same place.

quotes.text:
Whilst Palamon is with me, let me perish
If I think this our prison!
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 2 Scene 2
quotes.plain: With the right person beside you, the worst place stops feeling like a cage.

quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 2 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Two real friends are each other's whole world.

quotes.text:
I am sure, a more content; and all those pleasures
That woo the wills of men to vanity
I see through now, and am sufficient
To tell the world ’tis but a gaudy shadow
That old Time as he passes by takes with him.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 2 Scene 2
quotes.plain: Most of what tempts people is a shiny shadow that time carries off anyway.

quotes.text:
Come what can come,
The worst is death; I will not leave the kingdom.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 2 Scene 3
quotes.plain: Once you accept the worst case, you stop running from what you want.

quotes.text:
Their valiant temper
Men lose when they incline to treachery;
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 3 Scene 1
quotes.plain: Cut one corner on your own honor and the nerve goes out of you.

quotes.text:
Fortune, whose title is as momentary,
As to us death is certain.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Luck never holds a title for long. Death always does.

quotes.text:
And with our patience anger tottering Fortune,
Who at her certain’st reels.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Stay calm and luck gets rattled. Even at her best she is unsteady.

quotes.text:
That we should things desire, which do cost us
The loss of our desire! That naught could buy
Dear love, but loss of dear love!
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: Sometimes the price of the thing you want is the thing you wanted.

quotes.text:
What things you make of us! For what we lack
We laugh, for what we have are sorry, still
Are children in some kind. Let us be thankful
For that which is, and with you leave dispute
That are above our question.
quotes.location: The Two Noble Kinsmen, Act 5 Scene 4
quotes.plain: We want what we lack and grieve what we have. Be thankful for what is.

quotes.text:
Two lads that thought there was no more behind
But such a day tomorrow as today,
And to be boy eternal.
quotes.plain: Youth feels like every tomorrow will match today. It does not.

quotes.text: Temptations have since then been born to ’s!
quotes.plain: Innocence ends the day temptation shows up, and it always does.

quotes.text: Our praises are our wages.
quotes.plain: Praise is what people pay in. Don't work only for it.
The right company makes the long days short and clears the heavy thoughts.

quotes.text:
I may be negligent, foolish, and fearful;
In every one of these no man is free,
But that his negligence, his folly, fear,
Among the infinite doings of the world,
Sometime puts forth.
quotes.plain: Everybody is lazy, foolish and scared sometimes. Own it and keep going.

quotes.text:
I know not: but I am sure ’tis safer to
Avoid what’s grown than question how ’tis born.
quotes.plain: When trouble is already big, stop asking how it started and get out of the way.

quotes.text:
Alack, for lesser knowledge! How accurs’d
In being so blest! There may be in the cup
A spider steep’d, and one may drink, depart,
And yet partake no venom, for his knowledge
Is not infected; but if one present
Th’ abhorr’d ingredient to his eye, make known
How he hath drunk, he cracks his gorge, his sides,
With violent hefts. I have drunk, and seen the spider.
quotes.plain: Suspicion poisons you. Once you have seen the spider in the cup, you cannot unsee it.

quotes.text:
There’s some ill planet reigns:
I must be patient till the heavens look
With an aspect more favourable.
quotes.plain: Some seasons are just bad. Hold steady until the luck turns.

quotes.text:
The silence often of pure innocence
Persuades, when speaking fails.
quotes.plain: Sometimes quiet integrity wins what arguing can't.

quotes.text:
It is an heretic that makes the fire,
Not she which burns in ’t.
quotes.plain: The shame belongs to the one who lights the fire, not the one standing in it.

quotes.text: I am a feather for each wind that blows.
quotes.plain: No center, no direction. Every mood pushes you around.

quotes.text:
I doubt not, then, but innocence shall make
False accusation blush, and tyranny
Tremble at patience.
quotes.plain: Patience under false blame makes the accuser nervous.

quotes.text:
What’s gone and what’s past help,
Should be past grief.
quotes.plain: If you can't fix it, stop paying for it with your sleep.

quotes.text:
I that please some, try all: both joy and terror
Of good and bad, that makes and unfolds error,
Now take upon me, in the name of Time,
To use my wings.
quotes.plain: Time tests everyone, brings the good and the bad, and slides past whatever you hoped would stay.

quotes.text:
The selfsame sun that shines upon his court
Hides not his visage from our cottage, but
Looks on alike.
quotes.plain: The same sun shines on the palace and the shack. Power is not the same as worth.

quotes.text:
I am but sorry, not afeard; delay’d,
But nothing alt’red: what I was, I am:
More straining on for plucking back; not following
My leash unwillingly.
quotes.plain: Pulled back, not changed. The harder they yank the leash, the harder I pull forward.

quotes.text:
I think affliction may subdue the cheek,
But not take in the mind.
quotes.plain: Hardship can wear down your face. It only gets your mind if you let it in.

quotes.text: Ha, ha! what a fool Honesty is! and Trust, his sworn brother, a very simple gentleman!
quotes.plain: This is how a con man sees honest people. Don't be the easy mark.

quotes.text: I see this is the time that the unjust man doth thrive.
quotes.plain: Sometimes the crooked one is winning. Don't confuse that with being right.

quotes.text:
As every present time doth boast itself
Above a better gone, so must thy grave
Give way to what’s seen now!
quotes.plain: Every era brags it beats the last one, and the past always gets pushed aside.

quotes.text:
Scarce any joy
Did ever so long live; no sorrow
But kill’d itself much sooner.
quotes.plain: Even joy rarely lasts that long, and no sorrow does. This will wear itself out.

quotes.text:
When I do count the clock that tells the time,
And see the brave day sunk in hideous night,
When I behold the violet past prime,
And sable curls all silvered o’er with white:
quotes.plain: Watch the clock long enough and you see everything beautiful going gray. Use the days.

quotes.text:
When I consider everything that grows
Holds in perfection but a little moment.
quotes.plain: Everything at its peak only holds it for a short moment.

quotes.text:
Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
And summer’s lease hath all too short a date:
quotes.plain: Even the best season is on a short lease. Good things end fast.

quotes.text:
So long as men can breathe or eyes can see,
So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.
quotes.plain: What you make and put into the world can outlive you.

quotes.text:
Yet do thy worst, old Time; despite thy wrong,
My love shall in my verse ever live young.
quotes.plain: Time will take everything, but not what I put into my work. Do your worst.

quotes.text:
The painful warrior famoused for fight,
After a thousand victories once foiled,
Is from the book of honour razed quite,
And all the rest forgot for which he toiled:
quotes.plain: A thousand wins get wiped out by one loss. Don't build your worth on the record.

quotes.text:
Yet in these thoughts my self almost despising,
Haply I think on thee, and then my state,
(Like to the lark at break of day arising
From sullen earth) sings hymns at heaven’s gate,
For thy sweet love remembered such wealth brings,
That then I scorn to change my state with kings.
quotes.plain: Low and full of self-hate, then one good thought lifts you and you wouldn't trade places with a king.

quotes.text:
When to the sessions of sweet silent thought,
I summon up remembrance of things past,
I sigh the lack of many a thing I sought,
And with old woes new wail my dear time’s waste:
quotes.plain: In quiet you count every wasted year and every old loss all over again.

quotes.text:
No more be grieved at that which thou hast done,
Roses have thorns, and silver fountains mud,
Clouds and eclipses stain both moon and sun,
And loathsome canker lives in sweetest bud.
quotes.plain: Everything good has something ugly in it. Stop beating yourself up for your flaws.

quotes.text:
Like as the waves make towards the pebbled shore,
So do our minutes hasten to their end,
Each changing place with that which goes before,
In sequent toil all forwards do contend.
quotes.plain: Minutes roll in like waves, each one pushing the last aside. They don't wait.

quotes.text:
This thought is as a death which cannot choose
But weep to have, that which it fears to lose.
quotes.plain: The more you love something, the more the fear of losing it eats at you.

quotes.text:
That time of year thou mayst in me behold,
When yellow leaves, or none, or few do hang
Upon those boughs which shake against the cold,
Bare ruined choirs, where late the sweet birds sang.
quotes.plain: Late in life, the branches are bare where the birds used to sing.

quotes.text:
Thus have I had thee as a dream doth flatter,
In sleep a king, but waking no such matter.
quotes.plain: It felt like a kingdom in the dream. Then you wake up and it is gone.

quotes.text:
Some glory in their birth, some in their skill,
Some in their wealth, some in their body’s force,
Some in their garments though new-fangled ill:
Some in their hawks and hounds, some in their horse.
quotes.plain: Everyone brags about something: family, money, muscle, clothes, toys.

quotes.text:
They that have power to hurt, and will do none,
That do not do the thing, they most do show,
Who moving others, are themselves as stone,
Unmoved, cold, and to temptation slow:
quotes.plain: The strongest people could hurt you and don't. They stay cold to temptation.

quotes.text:
Take heed (dear heart) of this large privilege,
The hardest knife ill-used doth lose his edge.
quotes.plain: Misuse a sharp gift and it dulls. Talent wasted on junk goes blunt.

quotes.text:
Let me not to the marriage of true minds
Admit impediments, love is not love
Which alters when it alteration finds,
Or bends with the remover to remove.
O no, it is an ever-fixed mark
That looks on tempests and is never shaken;
It is the star to every wand’ring bark,
Whose worth’s unknown, although his height be taken.
quotes.plain: Real love does not move when things change. It is the fixed star you steer by in a storm.

quotes.text:
O benefit of ill, now I find true
That better is, by evil still made better.
quotes.plain: Getting burned made the good thing better. Trouble can improve what you rebuild.
I know who I am. The ones judging me are often crooked themselves.

quotes.text:
Mad in pursuit and in possession so,
Had, having, and in quest, to have extreme,
A bliss in proof, and proved, a very woe;
Before a joy proposed behind a dream.
quotes.plain: Wanting it drives you mad, having it ruins you, and before you get it it was only a dream.

quotes.text:
Poor soul the centre of my sinful earth,
My sinful earth these rebel powers array,
Why dost thou pine within and suffer dearth
Painting thy outward walls so costly gay?
quotes.plain: You starve the part of you that matters while spending everything on the outside.

quotes.text:
So shall thou feed on death, that feeds on men,
And death once dead, there’s no more dying then.
quotes.plain: Live for what lasts and death loses its hold on you.
